```text
CRITICAL!!: 
- NEVER EVER EVER create a branch!!! branches are FORBIDDEN!!!
- NEVER EVER EVER delete the `bugdrop-screenshots` branch, locally or remotely. It is protected project history.
- NEVER create a worktree, UNLESS the user has specifically asked for it!
- NEVER delete files unless the user has specifically asked for it. If you think a file is misplaced, unrelated, or stale, that is an entirely separate request — ask first. "Looks unrelated to this task" is not authorization to delete.

- When the user gives a UUID and asks what is going on with it, treat it as an OmniHarness conversation/session lookup: check `sqlite.db`, starting with the `runs` row for that UUID, then inspect related `workers`, `messages`, `execution_events`, queued messages, and validation/plan records as needed.
- To delete all conversations and associated persisted artifacts, use `scripts/delete-conversations.sh`

Testing:
- When testing the app, use the already-running process if one exists instead of starting another server.
- The normal runner URL is `http://localhost:3050`; the Vite development interface is usually at `http://localhost:5173`.
- Clean up any test sessions/conversations and their associated persisted artifacts before finishing.
- For lifecycle / chaos-style regressions (reconnect, restart, FK-on-delete, plan-review leftover state), use `pnpm test:lifecycle`. Scenarios live under `tests/lifecycle/scenarios/` and drive the control plane via HTTP/SSE — no Chromium. To debug a specific reported bug, mirror it as a new scenario file.
- Read `docs/architecture/lifecycle-observability-and-testing.md` before adding new server-side state transitions. It is the spec all new code is held to.
- Worker conversation content (direct-control and supervisor-driven worker turns) lives in the unified worker stream — one append-only JSONL per worker at `app-data/run-data/<runId>/<workerId>.jsonl`. Persist new worker content through `appendWorkerEntry` in `src/server/workers/output-store.ts`; render it through `WorkerEntriesManager` and the `entries` prop on `Terminal`. Do NOT add a parallel persistence layer (a sibling JSONL, a new `messages.kind`, an in-memory cache that the frontend reconciles against the stream). See `docs/architecture/worker-conversation-stream.md`.

Lifecycle observability rules (full doc: `docs/architecture/lifecycle-observability-and-testing.md`):
- Every server-side decision (spawn, reattach, recreate, give up, refuse, delete, fail) emits a typed named event via `emitNamedEvent` from `@/server/events/named-events`. Silent early returns and bare `catch {}` are bugs.
- User-relevant failures additionally emit `error.surfaced` with a stable `code` (typed union in `named-events.ts`), `surface`, and at least one relevant subject id such as `runId`/`workerId`/`conversationId`/`accountId`. Never funnel through a blanket wrapper in `api-errors.ts`.
- All SSE frames carry an `id:`. Clients reconnect with `Last-Event-ID`; the server replays from the ring buffer or emits `stream.resync_required`. Snapshot bootstrap is `GET /api/events?snapshot=1` (anchor id in the `x-omni-last-event-id` response header).
- Dev-only event log: `GET /api/events/log?since=<id>&runId=<id>` returns the ring buffer as JSON. Use this when triaging "X didn't happen" bug reports — if the event isn't there, the server didn't do the thing, and the next step is finding the silent branch.
- Chaos is a client-side concern. Never add fault-injection code paths to server code.

Frontend i18n:
- EVERY user-facing frontend string MUST live in `shared/locales/*.json` and be rendered with the `t()` function from `@/lib/i18n`.
- NEVER hardcode user-facing JSX text, button labels, dialog titles, aria-labels, titles, placeholders, empty states, status labels, help text, error fallback text, or visible option labels directly in components.
- For every new user-facing string, add the key to `shared/locales/en.json` and every other locale file in `shared/locales/` in the same change. Use stable dotted keys like `settings.runtime.recovery` or `conversation.sidebar.search`.
- Components that render translated strings and need to update when the language changes MUST subscribe to the i18n manager by calling `useI18nSnapshot()` from `@/lib/i18n`; then render text with the existing `t("key", params?)` function. The hook is only for re-rendering; `t()` is the translation API.
- Non-React modules that produce user-visible text must still use `t("key", params?)` at the boundary where text is produced. Protocol values, storage keys, API paths, CSS classes, model ids, and database values are not translation keys unless they are displayed as copy.
- Do not pass translated strings through transactions or persist translated UI copy. Store stable ids/values and translate at render time.

React Best Practices:
- MutableRefObject is deprecated in React; use RefObject instead.
- NEVER use require() to import modules. Use import instead.
- ALWAYS centralize all state in global single source of truth Manager classes. Components/listeners subscribe to updates from Managers and use Manager methods to update data.
- Always implement a custom data manager for any data structure. NEVER use separate state variables and arrays as the source of truth.
- NEVER send data around in transactions.
- Avoid using useEffect() to update state. Prefer useCallback() or Manager methods for explicit state transitions.
- Avoid callback hell, race conditions, and infinite loops.
- NEVER store string literals or UI settings for the frontend in the .env file. Use literals in files, inline arrays, or .json files instead.
- When debugging React: if a fix did not work, think hard about whether this is a race condition. Race conditions are common in React.
```

## Claude thinking · 2026-08-05T10:10:55.272Z

So the incident flow is: session missing triggers a policy that resumes from a saved session, marking it resolved with a continuation pending. When the continuation starts, it fails with an authentication error, which reopens the resolved incident and clears the resolution timestamp. After the user authenticates and sends a new message, the worker runs successfully, but something never completes.

The issue is that plain user turns don't interact with recovery incidents at all—only the recovery reconciler, quota resume logic, or explicit API routes handle resolution. I need to check the API route at runs.ts:268 to see what it does, and then look at the recovery reconciler around 440-520 to understand the resolution paths and whether it would re-evaluate the incident now that the session exists.

```text
14	  if (state.status === "recovering") return "recovery.notice.title.recovering";

16	  if (state.kind === "queue_blocked") return "recovery.notice.title.queueBlocked";
```

## Claude thinking · 2026-08-05T10:11:23.725Z

So the banner's behavior is tied entirely to `deriveRecoveryState`, which surfaces any incident marked as open, recovering, needs_user, or failed regardless of whether the run has progressed since then. The real issue is that `needs_user` incidents never get cleared when the user successfully resumes the conversation. I'm now tracing which code paths actually do close these incidents — user stops trigger settlement in runs.ts, quota workers handle their own incidents, and there are a few other recovery paths I'm still mapping out.

But here's the critical bug: when the reconciler classifies a run as healthy, it returns early without resolving any existing open incidents, leaving them dangling indefinitely. Meanwhile, the run's status itself gets reset somewhere in the send-message flow, so the run appears recovered to the user but the incidents remain unresolved in the system. I need to verify where that early return happens and whether the frontend has any way to dismiss the banner, plus check how the recovery policy classifies runs as healthy in the first place.

## Claude thinking · 2026-08-05T10:11:41.114Z

The real issue is that reconciliation only happens when the worker disappears, but once it comes back healthy, there's no mechanism to clean up those lingering incidents. I need to hook into the moment when the worker or run recovers—either after a successful worker turn or when the run status shifts back to running with an active worker—and auto-resolve any open incidents at that point. The challenge is finding the right place to intercept this, and `deriveRecoveryState` seems like a candidate, though I'm still evaluating the options.

## Claude · 2026-08-05T10:12:22.958Z

I traced it. This is a real bug, not a display glitch — the incident row is genuinely still open in the DB.

## What happened to `63b477920b47`

`sqlite.db` → `recovery_incidents`:

```
id      = aa8b614e-5024-4b90-8a84-e3cc32a55318
kind    = session_missing
status  = needs_user          ← still
last_error = Ask failed: Authentication required
resolved_at = (null)
detected_at = 1785919274
```

Meanwhile the run itself recovered fine: `runs.status = awaiting_user`, updated at `1785924572` (~88 min later).

The event trail shows the exact sequence:

1. `recovery_incident_opened` — `session_missing`, source `conversation-sync`
2. `recovery_policy_decision` — `resume_session`
3. `recovery_resolved` — session resumed, `continuationPending: true`
4. `recovery_continuation_started`
5. `recovery_continuation_failed` → `recovery_needs_user` — *"Ask failed: Authentication required"*

Step 5 is `src/server/runs/recovery-reconciler.ts:176`, which calls `markRecoveryIncidentNeedsUser` and deliberately clears `resolvedAt` (`recovery-incidents.ts:199`) to re-open the already-resolved incident. That part is correct. **Nothing ever closes it again.**

## Why it never clears

The banner is derived entirely from incident rows — `deriveRecoveryState` (`src/runtime/http/routes/events.ts:374`) picks any incident whose status is `open | recovering | needs_user | failed` and renders it. It never consults whether the run has since made progress.

And the only things that resolve an incident are:

| Path | Trigger |
|---|---|
| `runs.ts:268` | user explicitly **stops** the conversation |
| `recovery-reconciler.ts:452/511` | an **automatic** resume/restart succeeds |
| `quota/worker-resume.ts`, `type-blocking.ts` | quota incidents specifically |
| `supervisor/worker-failover.ts:421` | supervisor failover |

A user authenticating and simply sending another message hits none of these. Worse, `reconcileRunRecovery` isn't even called on the healthy path — `sync.ts:769` only invokes it when the worker is *missing* from the live agent list, and even when it does run, the healthy branch (`recovery-reconciler.ts:536`) early-returns `action: "none"` without touching lingering incidents. There's also no dismiss button on `RunRecoveryNotice.tsx`.

So a `needs_user` incident is a permanent tombstone unless you stop the conversation.

Same latent problem for `status = "failed"` incidents — `markRecoveryIncidentFailed` stamps `resolvedAt`, but `deriveRecoveryState` still counts `failed` as active, and `settleRunRecoveryAfterUserStop` only sweeps `open | recovering | needs_user`. That banner is unclearable by any route.

## Proposed fix

1. Add `resolveStaleRecoveryIncidentsForRun(runId, { workerId, reason })` to `recovery-incidents.ts` — sweeps `open | recovering | needs_user` to `resolved` with a `reason: "run_recovered"` detail, emitting the usual `recovery.resolved` named event so the lifecycle-observability rule is honoured.
2. Call it from the successful direct-turn completion path — `send-message.ts:696` and `queued-messages.ts:414`, next to `updateDirectRunStatusFromWorkerOutput`. A turn that completes without error *is* the proof the run recovered.
3. Belt-and-braces: call it in `reconcileRunRecovery`'s `state.kind === "healthy"` branch (`recovery-reconciler.ts:536`) instead of the bare early return — that branch is currently a silent early return, which `agents.md` flags as a bug in its own right.
4. Decide on `failed`: either drop it from `deriveRecoveryState`'s active set (it has a `resolvedAt` stamp, so it isn't active), or include it in the sweep. I'd sweep it — a later successful turn genuinely supersedes it.
5. Lifecycle scenario under `tests/lifecycle/scenarios/` mirroring this: open incident → mark `needs_user` → send a message that succeeds → assert `recoveryState` is null.

Two things I'd like your call on before touching anything:

- **Do you want me to implement this?** Your message reads as a complaint, and I don't act on ambiguous intent.
- **Clear the stuck row for `63b477920b47` right now?** A single `UPDATE recovery_incidents SET status='resolved', resolved_at=... WHERE id='aa8b614e-...'` kills the banner for your current session immediately, independent of the code fix.

## Claude thinking · 2026-08-05T10:15:03.200Z

The sweep logic needs to move to a better location—right after the worker status update succeeds, making it unconditional on run mode so it applies to planning runs too. I need to place it in send-message.ts after line 678 and in queued-messages.ts after line 411, plus handle the recovery-reconciler healthy branch and recovery continuation success path.

For the helper function, I should scope the incident sweep to both the run and the specific worker, since in multi-worker implementation runs, resolving another worker's incident just because one worker succeeded would be incorrect—even though quota exhaustion itself gets resolved when a turn succeeds, the incident might belong to a different worker. A successful worker turn proves the worker is reachable and authenticated, which invalidates incidents like `session_missing`, `worker_lost`, and `quota_exhausted` for that worker. I'll sweep all incident types for the matching worker plus any run-level incidents with null workerId, and let the reconciler re-open anything that's still genuinely broken — that way the system self-corrects through the normal incident reopening flow.

For `failed` incidents, sweeping them to `resolved` does lose the failure record in the row itself, but the execution events preserve the `recovery_exhausted` marker and the sweep creates its own event, so the history isn't completely lost. The tradeoff is worth it because it makes the banner clearable.

But there's another issue: `deriveRecoveryState` just grabs the first incident from the query without sorting, when it should be using the most recently updated one. Let me check how the incidents are ordered in the persisted-snapshot and events queries.

```text
import fs from "fs";
import os from "os";
import path from "path";
import { beforeEach } from "vitest";

// Never trust an inherited runner root here. Agent processes launched by a
// live OmniHarness runner inherit its OMNIHARNESS_ROOT; respecting that value
// would let ordinary test cleanup operate on the production database.
const testRoot = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "omniharness-tests-"));
process.env.OMNIHARNESS_ROOT = testRoot;

// Same hazard, one variable family further out. `applyProjectScopedCliStorage`
// deliberately yields to a caller-supplied CLI storage dir, and Claude worker
// startup yields to a caller-supplied ANTHROPIC_MODEL. Tests that assert the
// runtime pins storage under the project root, or pins an exact model, spread
// `...process.env` into the runtime they spawn — so whenever the suite runs
// from a shell that exports these (notably inside an agent CLI, which sets
// CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and ANTHROPIC_MODEL for its own session), the runtime took
// the yield branch and those tests failed on the developer's machine while
// passing in CI. Scrub them once, here, so no test can inherit them.
for (const key of [
  "ANTHROPIC_MODEL",
  "CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL",
  "CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR",
  "CODEX_HOME",
  "CODEX_SQLITE_HOME",
  "GEMINI_CLI_HOME",
  "OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR",
  "XDG_CACHE_HOME",
  "XDG_DATA_HOME",
  "XDG_STATE_HOME",
]) {
  delete process.env[key];
}

// Keep plan-readiness LLM judge off by default in tests. Individual tests can
// opt in by stubbing the module.
if (process.env.MOCK_LLM === undefined) {
  process.env.MOCK_LLM = "true";
}
```

```text
}

describe("steering an initial direct worker turn", () => {
  beforeEach(async () => {
    mockAskAgent.mockReset();
    mockCancelAgentTurn.mockReset();
    mockCancelAgentTurn.mockResolvedValue({ ok: true, name: "worker", cancelledPermissions: 0 });
    mockGetAgent.mockReset();
    mockSpawnAgent.mockReset();
    __resetWorkerTurnChainsForTests();

    await db.delete(executionEvents);
    await db.delete(queuedConversationMessages);
    await db.delete(messages);
    await db.delete(workers);
    await db.delete(workerCounters);
    await db.delete(runs);
    await db.delete(plans);
    await db.delete(settings);
  });

  it("does not record a user-requested steer abort as an initial worker failure", async () => {
    const initialAsk = deferred<{ response: string; state: string }>();
    mockAskAgent
      .mockReturnValueOnce(initialAsk.promise)
      .mockResolvedValueOnce({ response: "I am applying the fix now.", state: "idle" });
    mockSpawnAgent.mockImplementation(async ({ name, cwd }: { name: string; cwd: string }) => ({
      ...idleSnapshot(name),
      cwd,
      state: "working",
    }));
    mockGetAgent.mockImplementation(async (workerId: string) => idleSnapshot(workerId));

    const created = await createConversation({
      mode: "direct",
      command: "Find the scrolling bug, then ask before fixing it.",
      projectPath: process.cwd(),
      preferredWorkerType: "claude",
      allowedWorkerTypes: ["claude"],
    });
    const worker = await db.select().from(workers).where(eq(workers.runId, created.runId)).get();
    expect(worker).toBeDefined();

    const steer = await interruptWithDraftMessage({
      runId: created.runId,
      targetWorkerId: worker!.id,
      content: "yes fix",
      source: "api",
    });
    initialAsk.reject(new WorkerTurnAbortedError(worker!.id, "user steer"));
    await waitForConversationBackgroundTasksForTests();

    const storedRun = await db.select().from(runs).where(eq(runs.id, created.runId)).get();
    const storedQueue = await db
      .select()
      .from(queuedConversationMessages)
      .where(eq(queuedConversationMessages.id, steer.queuedMessage.id))
      .get();
    const events = await db.select().from(executionEvents).where(eq(executionEvents.runId, created.runId));

    expect(storedRun?.status).not.toBe("failed");
    expect(storedRun?.lastError).toBeNull();
    expect(storedQueue?.status).toBe("delivered");
    expect(events.some((event) => event.eventType === "run_failed")).toBe(false);
  });
});
```

## Claude · 2026-08-05T10:22:58.732Z

Fix implemented and verified.

## What changed

**`src/server/runs/recovery-incidents.ts`** — new `resolveRecoveryIncidentsAfterHealthyTurn(runId, workerId, summary, reason)`. Sweeps incidents in `open | recovering | needs_user | failed` to `resolved`, emitting the usual `recovery.resolved` named event plus an execution event per row. Scoped to the worker that just proved itself (plus run-level incidents naming no worker), so a healthy worker in a multi-worker implementation run can't clear a sibling's incident. `failed` is included because `deriveRecoveryState` renders it as active despite its `resolvedAt` stamp — that banner was previously unclearable by any route.

**Three call sites:**
- `send-message.ts:681` — after a worker turn completes normally
- `queued-messages.ts:413` — after a queued message is delivered normally
- `recovery-reconciler.ts:536` — the `healthy` branch, which was a bare silent early return (an `agents.md` violation in its own right). Only `healthy` sweeps; `recovering` is genuinely still in flight.

Anything still broken gets reopened by the next `openRecoveryIncident` call, so the sweep is self-correcting rather than authoritative.

## Verification

- `tests/server/conversations/recovery-incident-clearing.test.ts` — drives the real `sendConversationMessage` path with a mocked bridge, seeded with a `needs_user` incident carrying your exact `"Ask failed: Authentication required"` error. **I confirmed it fails when the call is removed from `send-message.ts`**, so it guards the wiring, not just the helper.
- `tests/lifecycle/scenarios/recovery-stale-needs-user.test.ts` — replays the field sequence (session_missing → resolved → continuation fails on auth → needs_user) and asserts `recoveryState` on the `/api/events` snapshot goes from `needs_user` to `null`. Plus the `failed`-incident case and the sibling-worker isolation case.
- `pnpm test:lifecycle`: 26 files, 37 tests, all pass.
- Recovery-adjacent server suites: 226 pass, 1 fail — `conversations-sync.test.ts > redelivers a queued answer as a normal prompt when the elicitation is already gone`. **I verified this fails identically on stashed HEAD**, so it predates this work and is unrelated.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean; eslint clean on changed files (2 pre-existing unused-type warnings in `queued-messages.ts`).

## Your session is still showing the banner

The running runner has the old code, and the incident row `aa8b614e-5024-4b90-8a84-e3cc32a55318` is still `needs_user` in `sqlite.db`. Two separate things are needed to actually clear your screen — neither is done:

```text
186	  private reconnectingAfterResync = false;
187	  private lastSnapshotPollAt = 0;
188	  private readonly cursor: LiveEventCursorManager;
189	  private connectionGeneration = 0;
190	
191	  constructor(options: LiveEventConnectionManagerOptions) {
192	    this.selectedRunId = options.selectedRunId;
193	    this.cursor = options.cursor ?? new LiveEventCursorManager(options.initialLastEventId);
194	    this.cursor.advance(options.initialLastEventId);
195	    this.events = options.events ?? createLegacyLiveEventAPIs({
196	      EventSourceConstructor: options.EventSourceConstructor,
197	      requestJson: options.requestJson,
198	      requestSnapshot: options.requestSnapshot,
199	    });
200	    this.getSnapshotChecksum = options.getSnapshotChecksum;
201	    this.workerEntries = options.workerEntries ?? workerEntriesManager;
202	    this.sidebarWorkerActivity = options.sidebarWorkerActivity ?? sidebarWorkerActivityManager;
203	    this.applyUpdate = options.applyUpdate;
204	    this.reportError = options.reportError;
205	    this.onStreamResync = options.onStreamResync;
206	    this.fallbackIntervalMs = options.fallbackIntervalMs ?? SNAPSHOT_FALLBACK_INTERVAL_MS;
207	    this.fallbackCooldownMs = options.fallbackCooldownMs ?? SNAPSHOT_FALLBACK_COOLDOWN_MS;
208	    this.snapshotValidationIntervalMs = options.snapshotValidationIntervalMs === undefined
209	      ? SNAPSHOT_VALIDATION_INTERVAL_MS
210	      : options.snapshotValidationIntervalMs;
211	  }
212	
213	  start() {
214	    if (this.active) {
215	      return;
216	    }
217	
218	    this.active = true;
219	    this.openEventSource();
220	
221	    this.startSnapshotValidation();
222	    void this.pollSnapshot({ force: true });
223	  }
224	
225	  private openEventSource() {
226	    this.eventSource = this.events.open({
227	      snapshot: false,
228	      runId: this.selectedRunId,
229	      lastEventId: this.cursor.getCurrent(),
230	    }, {
231	      onOpen: () => {
232	        this.stopFallbackPolling();
233	      },
234	      onEvent: (event) => {
235	        const streamEvent = event as {
236	          kind?: string;
237	          payload?: unknown;
238	          lastEventId?: string | null;
239	        };
240	        if (streamEvent.kind === "update") {
241	          this.handleUpdateEvent(streamEvent);
242	        } else if (streamEvent.kind === "update_error") {
243	          this.handleUpdateErrorEvent(streamEvent.payload);
244	        } else if (streamEvent.kind === "worker.entry_appended") {
245	          this.handleWorkerEntryAppended(streamEvent.payload);
246	        } else if (streamEvent.kind === "stream.resync_required") {
247	          void this.handleStreamResyncRequired();
248	        }
249	      },
250	      onError: () => {
251	        this.startFallbackPolling();
252	        void this.pollSnapshot({ force: true });
253	      },
254	    });
255	  }
256	
257	  stop() {
258	    this.active = false;
259	    this.connectionGeneration++;
260	    this.stopFallbackPolling();
261	    this.stopSnapshotValidation();
262	    this.eventSource?.close();
263	    this.eventSource = null;
264	  }
265	
266	  private handleUpdateEvent(event: { payload?: unknown; lastEventId?: string | null }) {
267	    try {
268	      if (event.lastEventId && !this.cursor.advance(event.lastEventId)) {
269	        return;
270	      }
271	      const data = event.payload as EventStreamState;
272	      if (!data || typeof data !== "object") {
273	        throw new TypeError("Invalid live update.");
274	      }
275	      this.stopFallbackPolling();
276	      this.applyUpdate(data);
277	      this.workerEntries.onKnownSeqs(data.workerEntrySeqs);
278	      this.sidebarWorkerActivity.onKnownSeqs(data.workerEntrySeqs);
279	    } catch {
280	      this.reportError({
281	        message: "The frontend received a malformed live update payload.",
282	        source: "Events",
283	        action: "Process live updates",
284	        suggestion: "Inspect the events route response payload and server logs, then refresh the page after fixing the malformed data.",
285	      });
286	    }
287	  }
288	
289	  private handleWorkerEntryAppended(payload: unknown) {
290	    try {
291	      const data = payload as { workerId?: unknown; seq?: unknown; runId?: unknown };
292	      const workerId = typeof data.workerId === "string" ? data.workerId : null;
293	      const seq = typeof data.seq === "number" ? data.seq : null;
294	      const runId = typeof data.runId === "string" ? data.runId : null;
295	      if (!workerId || seq == null) {
296	        return;
297	      }
298	      this.workerEntries.onWakeUp({ workerId, seq });
299	      this.sidebarWorkerActivity.onWakeUp({ workerId, seq, runId });
300	    } catch {
301	      // Malformed frames are ignored — the next valid frame (or the
302	      // periodic snapshot poll) will re-sync any missed entries.
303	    }
304	  }
305	
306	  private handleUpdateErrorEvent(payload: unknown) {
307	    try {
308	      this.reportError(withFallbackErrorContext(payload, {
309	        source: "Events",
310	        action: "Stream live updates",
311	      }));
312	    } catch {
313	      this.reportError({
314	        message: "The live event stream reported a malformed error payload.",
315	        source: "Events",
316	        action: "Stream live updates",
317	      });
318	    }
319	
320	    this.startFallbackPolling();
321	    void this.pollSnapshot({ force: true });
322	  }
323	
324	  private async handleStreamResyncRequired() {
325	    this.workerEntries.onStreamResync();
326	    this.onStreamResync?.();
327	    if (!this.active || this.reconnectingAfterResync) {
328	      return;
329	    }
330	
331	    this.reconnectingAfterResync = true;
332	    this.eventSource?.close();
333	    this.eventSource = null;
334	    this.cursor.clear();
335	    try {
336	      const snapshotLoaded = await this.pollSnapshot({ force: true });
337	      if (!this.active || !snapshotLoaded) {
338	        this.startFallbackPolling();
339	        return;
340	      }
341	
342	      this.openEventSource();
343	    } finally {
344	      this.reconnectingAfterResync = false;
345	    }
346	  }
347	
348	  private startFallbackPolling() {
349	    if (this.fallbackTimer) {
350	      return;
351	    }
352	
353	    this.fallbackTimer = setInterval(() => {
354	      void this.pollSnapshot();
355	    }, this.fallbackIntervalMs);
356	  }
357	
358	  private stopFallbackPolling() {
359	    if (!this.fallbackTimer) {
360	      return;
361	    }
362	
363	    clearInterval(this.fallbackTimer);
364	    this.fallbackTimer = null;
365	  }
366	
367	  private startSnapshotValidation() {
368	    if (
369	      this.snapshotValidationTimer
370	      || this.snapshotValidationIntervalMs == null
371	      || this.snapshotValidationIntervalMs <= 0
372	    ) {
373	      return;
374	    }
375	
376	    this.snapshotValidationTimer = setInterval(() => {
377	      void this.pollSnapshot();
378	    }, this.snapshotValidationIntervalMs);
379	  }
380	
381	  private stopSnapshotValidation() {
382	    if (!this.snapshotValidationTimer) {
383	      return;
384	    }
385	
386	    clearInterval(this.snapshotValidationTimer);
387	    this.snapshotValidationTimer = null;
388	  }
389	
390	  private async pollSnapshot(options: { force?: boolean } = {}): Promise<boolean> {
391	    if (this.pollingSnapshot) {
392	      return this.snapshotPollPromise ?? Promise.resolve(false);
393	    }
394	
395	    const now = Date.now();
396	    if (
397	      !this.active
398	      || (!options.force && now - this.lastSnapshotPollAt < this.fallbackCooldownMs)
399	    ) {
400	      return false;
401	    }
402	
403	    this.lastSnapshotPollAt = now;
404	    this.pollingSnapshot = true;
405	    this.snapshotPollPromise = this.runSnapshotPoll();
406	    try {
407	      return await this.snapshotPollPromise;
408	    } finally {
409	      this.pollingSnapshot = false;
410	      this.snapshotPollPromise = null;
411	    }
412	  }
413	
414	  private async runSnapshotPoll(): Promise<boolean> {
415	    const gen = this.connectionGeneration;
416	    try {
417	      const result = await this.events.snapshot({
418	        runId: this.selectedRunId,
419	        persisted: true,
420	        checksum: this.getSnapshotChecksum?.() ?? null,
421	      }) as SnapshotPollResult;
422	      if (!this.active || gen !== this.connectionGeneration) {
423	        return false;
424	      }
425	      this.setLastEventId(result.lastEventId);
426	      const data = result.data;
427	      if (isNotModifiedSnapshot(data)) {
428	        this.workerEntries.onKnownSeqs(data.workerEntrySeqs);
429	        this.sidebarWorkerActivity.onKnownSeqs(data.workerEntrySeqs);
430	        return true;
431	      }
432	      this.applyUpdate(data);
433	      this.workerEntries.onKnownSeqs(data?.workerEntrySeqs);
434	      this.sidebarWorkerActivity.onKnownSeqs(data?.workerEntrySeqs);
435	      return true;
436	    } catch (error) {
437	      if (this.active) {
438	        if (isTransientConnectivityError(error)) {
439	          return false;
440	        }
441	
442	        this.reportError(withFallbackErrorContext(error, {
443	          source: "Events",
444	          action: "Load live state snapshot",
445	        }));
446	      }
447	      return false;
448	    }
449	  }
450	
451	  private setLastEventId(lastEventId: string | number | null | undefined) {
452	    this.cursor.advance(lastEventId);
453	  }
454	}
```

```text
13	function sortMessages(messages: MessageRecord[]) {

22	function mergeByKey<T>(current: T[] | undefined, incoming: T[] | undefined, getKey: (item: T) => string | null | undefined) {
23	  const incomingItems = incoming ?? [];
24	  const seen = new Set<string>();
25	  const merged: T[] = [];
26	
27	  for (const item of incomingItems) {
28	    const key = getKey(item);
29	    if (key) {
30	      seen.add(key);
31	    }
32	    merged.push(item);
33	  }

35	  for (const item of current ?? []) {
36	    const key = getKey(item);
37	    if (!key || seen.has(key)) {
38	      continue;
39	    }
40	    seen.add(key);
41	    merged.push(item);
42	  }
43	
44	  return merged;
45	}

61	function mergeReadMarkersForVisibleRuns(current: EventStreamState, incoming: EventStreamState) {
62	  const visibleRunIds = new Set((incoming.runs ?? []).map((run) => run.id));
63	  const merged: Record<string, string> = {};
64	
65	  for (const [runId, readAt] of Object.entries(current.readMarkers ?? {})) {

68	    }
69	  }
70	
71	  for (const [runId, readAt] of Object.entries(incoming.readMarkers ?? {})) {
72	    if (!visibleRunIds.has(runId)) {
73	      continue;
74	    }
75	    if (timestampMs(readAt) >= timestampMs(merged[runId])) {

83	function mergeScopedCatalog(current: EventStreamState, incoming: EventStreamState) {
84	  const isSelectedRunScoped = Boolean(incoming.snapshotRunId?.trim());
85	  const catalogIsPartial = incoming.snapshotScope?.catalog?.complete === false;
86	  if (!isSelectedRunScoped && !catalogIsPartial) {

88	      ...incoming,
89	      readMarkers: mergeReadMarkersForVisibleRuns(current, incoming),

91	  }
92	
93	  const mergedRuns = mergeByKey(current.runs, incoming.runs, (run) => run.id);

99	    sessions: mergeByKey(current.sessions, incoming.sessions, (session) => session.runId),
100	    readMarkers: mergeReadMarkersForVisibleRuns(current, {

102	      runs: mergedRuns,
103	    }),

107	function mergeScopedRuns(current: EventStreamState, incoming: EventStreamState, options: {
108	  serverAuthoritative: boolean;

111	  if (options.serverAuthoritative) {

113	  }

115	  const incomingRuns = catalogMergedIncoming.runs ?? [];
116	  if (incomingRuns.length === 0 || !current.runs?.length) {

125	      return incomingRun;
126	    }
127	
128	    changed = true;
129	    return {
130	      ...incomingRun,
131	      ...currentRun,
132	    };
133	  });

145	function mergeScopedMessages(current: EventStreamState, incoming: EventStreamState) {
146	  const incomingMessages = incoming.messages ?? [];

148	  const completeMessageRunIds = new Set(

152	  const retainedCurrentMessages = (current.messages ?? []).filter((message) => (
153	    liveRunIds.has(message.runId)

155	    && !completeMessageRunIds.has(message.runId)

225	function mergeScopedCachedState(current: EventStreamState, cached: EventStreamState): EventStreamState {
226	  // hydrateFromCacheScope swaps scopes (e.g. on session switch). The cached
227	  // payload for the newly-selected scope only contains data that was

239	  // consumers gating on snapshotRunId still recognize the switch.

243	    snapshotChecksum: cached.snapshotChecksum ?? current.snapshotChecksum,

258	/**
259	 * State manager for the global event snapshot stream. Worker
260	 * conversation content (bridge entries, user/supervisor inputs,
261	 * lifecycle markers) is NOT managed here — it lives in
262	 * `WorkerEntriesManager` and is fetched per-worker via
263	 * the typed worker-entry API. This manager owns runs, plans,
264	 * workers metadata, supervisor messages, planning artifacts, queued
265	 * messages, recovery state, and review records.
266	 */
267	export class EventStreamStateManager {
268	  private state: EventStreamState;
269	  private readonly listeners = new Set<EventStreamStateListener>();
270	  private readonly snapshotCache: EventStreamSnapshotCacheManager;
271	  private snapshotCacheScope: string | null;
272	
273	  constructor(initialState: EventStreamState, options: {
274	    snapshotCache?: EventStreamSnapshotCacheManager;
275	    snapshotCacheScope?: string | null;
276	    deferCacheHydration?: boolean;
277	    initialSnapshotSource?: EventStreamSnapshotSource;
278	  } = {}) {
279	    this.snapshotCache = options.snapshotCache ?? new EventStreamSnapshotCacheManager();
280	    this.snapshotCacheScope = options.snapshotCacheScope?.trim() || null;
281	    const source = options.initialSnapshotSource;
282	    const initialWithSource = source ? { ...initialState, snapshotSource: source } : initialState;
283	    if (options.deferCacheHydration) {
284	      this.state = initialWithSource;
285	    } else {
286	      this.state = {
287	        ...this.snapshotCache.hydrateState(initialWithSource, this.snapshotCacheScope),
288	        snapshotSource: "cache",
289	      };
290	    }
291	  }
292	
293	  hydrateFromCaches() {
294	    if (authoritativeCatalogExcludesScope(this.state, this.snapshotCacheScope)) {
295	      return;
296	    }
297	    if (
298	      this.state.snapshotSource === "server"
299	      && (!this.snapshotCacheScope || this.state.snapshotRunId === this.snapshotCacheScope)
300	    ) {
301	      return;
302	    }
303	    const cached = this.snapshotCache.hydrateState(this.state, this.snapshotCacheScope);
304	    if (cached === this.state) {
305	      return;
306	    }
307	    this.state = { ...cached, snapshotSource: "cache" };
308	    for (const listener of this.listeners) {
309	      listener(this.state);
310	    }
311	  }
312	
313	  hydrateFromCacheScope(scope: string | null | undefined) {
314	    this.snapshotCacheScope = scope?.trim() || null;
315	    if (authoritativeCatalogExcludesScope(this.state, this.snapshotCacheScope)) {
316	      return false;
317	    }
318	    if (
319	      this.state.snapshotSource === "server"
320	      && this.snapshotCacheScope
321	      && this.state.snapshotRunId === this.snapshotCacheScope

324	    }
325	    const cached = this.snapshotCache.getCachedState(this.snapshotCacheScope);
326	    if (!cached || Object.is(cached, this.state)) {
327	      return false;
328	    }
329	
330	    this.state = {
331	      ...mergeScopedCachedState(this.state, cached),
332	      snapshotSource: this.state.snapshotSource === "server" ? "server" : "cache",
333	    };
334	    for (const listener of this.listeners) {
335	      listener(this.state);
336	    }
337	    return true;
338	  }
339	
340	  getSnapshot() {

342	  }
343	
344	  subscribe(listener: EventStreamStateListener) {

350	
351	  setSnapshotCacheScope(scope: string | null | undefined) {

353	  }

355	  update(action: EventStreamStateAction, options: { snapshotSource?: EventStreamSnapshotSource } = {}) {
356	    const incoming = typeof action === "function" ? action(this.state) : action;
357	    const snapshotSource = options.snapshotSource
358	      ?? incoming.snapshotSource
359	      ?? this.state.snapshotSource;
360	    const incomingWithRuns = mergeScopedRuns(this.state, incoming, {
361	      serverAuthoritative: snapshotSource === "server",
362	    });
363	    const incomingWithAgents = mergeDegradedAgentHumanInput(this.state, incomingWithRuns);
364	    const nextState = {
365	      ...mergeScopedMessages(this.state, incomingWithAgents),
366	      snapshotSource,
367	    };

369	    if (Object.is(nextState, this.state)) {
370	      return this.state;
371	    }
372	
373	    this.state = nextState;
374	    this.snapshotCache.rememberState(nextState, this.snapshotCacheScope);
375	    this.listeners.forEach((listener) => listener(this.state));

377	  }

379	  /**
380	   * Apply an explicit local mutation without treating its intentionally
381	   * removed records as a partial server catalog that needs merging.
382	   */
383	  updateLocal(action: EventStreamStateAction) {
384	    const incoming = typeof action === "function" ? action(this.state) : action;
385	    const nextState = {
386	      ...incoming,
387	      snapshotSource: this.state.snapshotSource,
388	    };
389	    if (Object.is(nextState, this.state)) {
390	      return this.state;
391	    }
392	    this.state = nextState;
393	    this.snapshotCache.rememberState(nextState, this.snapshotCacheScope);
394	    this.listeners.forEach((listener) => listener(this.state));
395	    return this.state;
396	  }
397	
398	  updateFromServer(action: EventStreamStateAction) {
399	    return this.update(action, { snapshotSource: "server" });
```

```text
7	// The event stream pushes a fresh snapshot for every agent output change,

94	export class EventStreamSnapshotCacheManager {
95	  private readonly storage: SnapshotStorage | null;

99	  private readonly now: () => number;

102	  private flushTimer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null;
103	
104	  constructor(options: EventStreamSnapshotCacheManagerOptions = {}) {
105	    const usesDefaultStorage = options.storage === undefined;
106	    this.storage = usesDefaultStorage ? getDefaultStorage() : options.storage ?? null;
107	    this.storageKey = options.storageKey ?? DEFAULT_STORAGE_KEY;
108	    this.maxSnapshots = options.maxSnapshots ?? DEFAULT_MAX_SNAPSHOTS;
109	    this.maxSerializedBytes = options.maxSerializedBytes ?? DEFAULT_MAX_SERIALIZED_BYTES;
110	    this.now = options.now ?? Date.now;
```

```text
1	import { StateManager } from "@/lib/state-manager";
2	import type { HomeUiState } from "./HomeUiStateManager";
3	
4	export class AutoResumeExhaustionManager extends StateManager<Set<string>> {
5	  constructor() {
6	    super(new Set());
7	  }
8	
9	  clear(runId: string) {
10	    this.update((current) => {
11	      if (!current.has(runId)) return current;
12	      const next = new Set(current);
13	      next.delete(runId);
14	      return next;
15	    });
16	  }
17	
18	  mark(runId: string) {
19	    this.update((current) => {
20	      if (current.has(runId)) return current;
21	      return new Set(current).add(runId);
22	    });
23	  }
24	}
25	
26	export const autoResumeExhaustionManager = new AutoResumeExhaustionManager();
27	
28	export type HomeAppState = Omit<
29	  HomeUiState,
30	  "command" | "commandCursor" | "mentionIndex" | "attachments"
31	>;
32	
33	export function selectHomeAppState(state: HomeUiState): HomeAppState {
34	  const selected: Partial<HomeUiState> = { ...state };
35	  delete selected.command;
36	  delete selected.commandCursor;
37	  delete selected.mentionIndex;
38	  delete selected.attachments;
39	  return selected as HomeAppState;
40	}
41	
42	function timestampMs(value: string | null | undefined) {
43	  if (!value) {
44	    return 0;
45	  }
46	  const parsed = new Date(value).getTime();
47	  return Number.isFinite(parsed) ? parsed : 0;
48	}
49	
50	export function mergeReadMarkers(
51	  persisted: Record<string, string> | null | undefined,
52	  optimistic: Record<string, string>,
53	) {
54	  const merged = { ...(persisted ?? {}) };
55	  for (const [runId, readAt] of Object.entries(optimistic)) {
56	    if (timestampMs(readAt) >= timestampMs(merged[runId])) {
57	      merged[runId] = readAt;
58	    }
59	  }
60	  return merged;
61	}
```

```text
You are investigating a UI performance problem in the OmniHarness repo at /Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness. Symptom: when MULTIPLE agent sessions are in flight, the React UI is slow to scroll, slow to click question/permission forms, and sometimes freezes.

DO NOT MODIFY ANY FILES. This is read-only analysis. Report findings only.

Your assigned area: the conversation transcript / worker output rendering — the biggest DOM surface.

Read and analyze in detail:
- src/components/home/ConversationMain.tsx (1563 lines)
- src/interface/home/WorkerEntriesManager.ts (909 lines)
- src/interface/home/ConversationTranscriptManager.ts
- the Terminal component and its `entries` prop (find it)
- src/interface/home/direct-worker-stream-loading.ts
- any markdown/syntax-highlight rendering in the entry path

Answer these specific questions with file:line evidence:
1. Is the transcript virtualized (windowed) at all, or does it render EVERY entry to the DOM? How many DOM nodes for a long conversation? Look for react-window/react-virtual/virtuoso in package.json — is any present and actually used?
2. Are entry components memoized (React.memo / useMemo)? When one new entry streams in, do ALL previous entries re-render? Trace prop identity — are new array/object identities created every render?
3. Is markdown parsing / syntax highlighting done on every render rather than cached per entry? Find the highlighter and check for memoization. This is a classic main-thread freeze source.
4. Does ConversationMain render data for NON-selected conversations/workers? Look for maps over all runs or all workers.
5. Are there expensive synchronous operations in render (JSON.parse, regex over large strings, .sort on big arrays, date formatting per entry)?
6. Check the auto-scroll implementation — does it force synchronous layout (scrollHeight/offsetHeight reads) on every frame? Layout thrashing is a top cause of scroll jank.

Be concrete and quantitative. Cite file:line for every claim. Rank findings by likely impact on click latency / scroll jank / freezes. Your final message is the return value — a dense technical report, no preamble.

uuid: 6f6fdb51-a53b-479e-8e72-f7a34b791305
```

```text
1	type LiveUpdateListener = () => void;
2	type EventStreamWaitResult = {
3	  notified: boolean;
4	};
5	
6	const listeners = new Set<LiveUpdateListener>();
7	let notificationVersion = 0;
8	
9	export function notifyEventStreamSubscribers() {
10	  notificationVersion += 1;
11	  for (const listener of listeners) {
12	    listener();
13	  }
14	}
15	
16	export function getEventStreamNotificationVersion() {
17	  return notificationVersion;
18	}
19	
20	export function waitForEventStreamNotification(timeoutMs: number, afterVersion = notificationVersion) {
21	  return new Promise<EventStreamWaitResult>((resolve) => {
22	    if (notificationVersion > afterVersion) {
23	      resolve({ notified: true });
24	      return;
25	    }
26	
27	    let settled = false;
28	    let timeout: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null;
29	
30	    const cleanup = (result: EventStreamWaitResult) => {
31	      if (settled) {
32	        return;
33	      }
34	
35	      settled = true;
36	      if (timeout) {
37	        clearTimeout(timeout);
38	      }
39	      listeners.delete(listener);
40	      resolve(result);
41	    };
42	
43	    const listener = () => cleanup({ notified: true });
44	    listeners.add(listener);
45	    timeout = setTimeout(() => cleanup({ notified: false }), timeoutMs);
46	  });
47	}
48
```

```text
298	function compactExecutionEventDetails(details: string | null) {
299	  if (!details?.trim()) {
300	    return details ?? null;
301	  }
302	
303	  try {
304	    const parsed = JSON.parse(details) as Record<string, unknown>;
305	    const compacted: Record<string, unknown> = {};
306	
307	    for (const key of [
308	      "summary",
309	      "reason",
310	      "error",
311	      "mode",
312	      "seconds",
313	      "recoveryState",
314	      "recommendedAction",
315	      "resetAt",
316	      "resumeAt",
317	      "scheduledWakeAt",
318	      "quotaResetSource",
319	      "quotaResetConfidence",
320	      "retryAfterMs",
321	      "provider",
322	      "sourceType",
323	      "rawText",
324	    ]) {
325	      const value = parsed[key];
326	      if (typeof value === "string") {
327	        compacted[key] = truncateText(value, EXECUTION_EVENT_DETAIL_LIMIT);
328	      } else if (typeof value === "number") {
329	        compacted[key] = value;
330	      }
331	    }
332	
333	    return Object.keys(compacted).length > 0 ? JSON.stringify(compacted) : "{}";
334	  } catch {
335	    return JSON.stringify({
336	      summary: truncateText(details, EXECUTION_EVENT_DETAIL_LIMIT),
337	    });
338	  }
339	}

374	function deriveRecoveryState(incidents: PersistedEventRecords["allRecoveryIncidents"]) {
375	  const active = incidents.find((incident) => (
376	    incident.status === "open"
377	    || incident.status === "recovering"
378	    || incident.status === "needs_user"
379	    || incident.status === "failed"
380	  ));
381	  if (!active) {
382	    return null;
383	  }
384	
385	  let parsedDetails: Record<string, unknown> = {};
386	  try {
387	    parsedDetails = active.details ? JSON.parse(active.details) as Record<string, unknown> : {};
388	  } catch {
389	    parsedDetails = {};
390	  }
391	
392	  return {
393	    kind: String(parsedDetails.recoveryState ?? active.kind),
394	    status: active.status,
395	    workerId: active.workerId,
396	    queuedMessageId: active.queuedMessageId,
397	    message: typeof parsedDetails.reason === "string" ? parsedDetails.reason : active.lastError,
398	    recommendedAction: String(parsedDetails.recommendedAction ?? (
399	      active.status === "recovering" ? "none" : "manual_resume"
400	    )),
401	    lastError: active.lastError,
402	    attemptCount: active.autoAttemptCount,
403	    nextAttemptAt: typeof parsedDetails.nextAttemptAt === "string" ? parsedDetails.nextAttemptAt : null,
404	    resumeAt: typeof parsedDetails.resumeAt === "string" ? parsedDetails.resumeAt : null,
405	    quotaResetSource: typeof parsedDetails.quotaResetSource === "string" ? parsedDetails.quotaResetSource : null,
406	    quotaResetConfidence: typeof parsedDetails.quotaResetConfidence === "string" ? parsedDetails.quotaResetConfidence : null,
407	    policyDecision: typeof parsedDetails.decision === "string" ? parsedDetails.decision : null,
408	  };

411	function compactAgentSnapshot(agent: ReturnType<typeof buildLiveWorkerSnapshots>[number]) {
412	  // Worker conversation content (outputEntries) is no longer carried
413	  // on the /api/events snapshot. Clients fetch it via
414	  // /api/workers/:workerId/entries through `WorkerEntriesManager`. The
415	  // agents[] array stays for non-content metadata: state, the
416	  // "thinking…" indicator, bridge-missing flag, last error.
417	  return {
418	    ...agent,

422	    lastText: truncateText(agent.lastText, AGENT_TEXT_FIELD_LIMIT),
423	    outputLog: truncateText(agent.outputLog, AGENT_TEXT_FIELD_LIMIT),
424	    displayText: truncateText(agent.displayText, AGENT_TEXT_FIELD_LIMIT),
425	    stderrBuffer: (agent.stderrBuffer ?? []).slice(-10).map((line) => truncateText(line, 2_000)),
426	  };

429	async function buildWorkerEntrySeqs(workers: Array<{ id: string; runId: string }>) {
430	  const seqs = await Promise.all(
431	    workers.map(async (worker) => {
432	      const seq = await readWorkerLatestSeq(worker.runId, worker.id);
433	      return seq > 0 ? [worker.id, seq] as const : null;

439	function filterRuntimeAgentsForWorkers(rawAgents: unknown[], scopedWorkers: PersistedEventRecords["allWorkers"]) {
440	  const workerIds = new Set(scopedWorkers.map((worker) => worker.id));
441	  if (workerIds.size === 0) {
442	    return [];
443	  }
444	
445	  return rawAgents.filter((agent) => {
446	    if (typeof agent !== "object" || agent === null) {
447	      return false;
448	    }
449	
450	    const name = (agent as { name?: unknown }).name;
451	    return typeof name === "string" && workerIds.has(name);
452	  });
453	}

455	function buildEventPayload(
456	  records: PersistedEventRecords,
457	  agentsData: ReturnType<typeof buildLiveWorkerSnapshots>,
458	  frontendErrors: AppErrorPayload[] = [],
459	  options: EventPayloadOptions = {},
460	  workerEntrySeqs: Record<string, number> = {},
461	  claudeModelGateway = getClaudeModelGatewayService().getSnapshot(),
462	) {
463	  const selectedRunId = resolveVisibleSelectedRunId(records, options);
464	  const runIds = visibleSelectedRunIds(records, options);
465	  const messageRunIds = selectedMessageRunIds(records, options);
466	  const lifecycleErrors = buildAwaitingUserQuestionInvariantErrors({
467	    runs: records.allRuns,
468	    messages: records.msgs,
469	    clarifications: records.allClarifications,
470	    selectedRunId: options.selectedRunId,
471	  });
472	  const processSessionsByRunId = new Map<string, PersistedEventRecords["allProcessSessions"][number]>(
473	    records.allProcessSessions.map((session) => [session.runId, session]),
474	  );
475	  const workersByRunId = new Map<string, PersistedEventRecords["allWorkers"][number]>();
476	  for (const worker of records.allWorkers) {
477	    if (!workersByRunId.has(worker.runId)) {
478	      workersByRunId.set(worker.runId, worker);
479	    }
480	  }
481	  const sessions = records.allRuns.map((run) => serializeSessionRecord({
482	    run,
483	    primaryWorker: workersByRunId.get(run.id) ?? null,
484	    processSession: processSessionsByRunId.get(run.id) ?? null,
485	  }));
486	  const readMarkers = Object.fromEntries(
487	    records.allReadMarkers.map((marker) => [marker.runId, marker.lastReadAt.toISOString()]),
488	  );
489	  // Worker conversation content now lives in the unified worker stream
490	  // (per-worker JSONL, fetched via /api/workers/:workerId/entries). The
491	  // previous `synthesizeStreamingWorkerMessages` path that fabricated
492	  // pseudo-messages from `agent.outputEntries` is gone; clients render
493	  // worker content via `WorkerEntriesManager` instead.
494	  return withEventPayloadChecksum({
495	    messages: records.msgs.map(serializeMessageRecord),
496	    readMarkers,
497	    plans: records.allPlans,
498	    runs: records.allRuns,
499	    sessions,
500	    accounts: records.allAccounts.map(toAccountDto),
501	    agents: agentsData.map(compactAgentSnapshot),
502	    workers: records.allWorkers.map(compactWorkerRecord),
503	    planItems: records.allPlanItems,
504	    clarifications: records.allClarifications,
505	    executionEvents: records.allExecutionEvents
506	      .slice(0, EXECUTION_EVENT_LIMIT)
507	      .map(compactExecutionEvent),
508	    supervisorInterventions: records.allSupervisorInterventions
509	      .map(compactSupervisorIntervention),
510	    queuedMessages: records.allQueuedMessages
511	      .filter((message) => message.status === "pending" || message.status === "delivering")
512	      .map(serializeQueuedConversationMessage),
513	    recoveryIncidents: records.allRecoveryIncidents
514	      .map(compactRecoveryIncident),
515	    recoveryState: runIds && !isTerminalRunStatus(
516	      records.allRuns.find((run) => runIds.has(run.id))?.status,
517	    )
518	      ? deriveRecoveryState(records.allRecoveryIncidents)
519	      : null,
520	    reviewRuns: records.allReviewRuns,
521	    reviewRounds: records.allReviewRounds,
522	    reviewFindings: records.allReviewFindings
523	      .map(compactReviewFinding),
524	    frontendErrors: [...frontendErrors, ...lifecycleErrors],
525	    snapshotRunId: selectedRunId,
526	    messageScope: {
527	      runIds: messageRunIds,
528	      complete: true,
529	    },
530	    // Bounded selected-run collections: list a cursor + completeness
531	    // flag so the UI can distinguish "full transcript loaded" from
532	    // "preview/tail only" and trigger pagination if it wants the rest.
533	    // Artifact-backed payloads MAY be partial; the cursor lets a
534	    // follow-up query request older entries.
535	    snapshotScope: {
536	      catalog: {
537	        complete: true,
538	      },
539	      executionEvents: {
540	        limit: EXECUTION_EVENT_LIMIT,
541	        complete: records.allExecutionEvents.length < EXECUTION_EVENT_LIMIT,
542	        oldestCreatedAt: records.allExecutionEvents.length > 0
543	          ? records.allExecutionEvents[records.allExecutionEvents.length - 1]!.createdAt.toISOString()
544	          : null,
545	      },
546	      supervisorInterventions: {
547	        limit: SUPERVISOR_INTERVENTION_LIMIT,
548	        complete: records.allSupervisorInterventions.length < SUPERVISOR_INTERVENTION_LIMIT,
549	        oldestCreatedAt: records.allSupervisorInterventions.length > 0
550	          ? records.allSupervisorInterventions[records.allSupervisorInterventions.length - 1]!.createdAt.toISOString()
551	          : null,
552	      },
553	      planningReviewFindings: {
554	        limit: PLANNING_REVIEW_FINDING_LIMIT,
555	        complete: records.allReviewFindings.length < PLANNING_REVIEW_FINDING_LIMIT,
556	        oldestCreatedAt: records.allReviewFindings.length > 0
557	          ? records.allReviewFindings[records.allReviewFindings.length - 1]!.createdAt.toISOString()
558	          : null,
559	      },
560	    },
561	    workerEntrySeqs,
562	    claudeModelGateway,
563	  });
564	}

566	async function buildPersistedEventPayload(options: EventPayloadOptions = {}, probe?: { mark: (label: string) => void }) {
567	  const records = await readPersistedEventRecords(options, probe);
568	  probe?.mark("readRecords.total");
569	  const scopedWorkers = selectedRunWorkers(records, options);
570	  const workerEntrySeqs = await buildWorkerEntrySeqs(scopedWorkers);
571	  probe?.mark(`workerSeqs[${scopedWorkers.length}]`);
572	  const payload = buildEventPayload(
573	    records,
574	    buildLiveWorkerSnapshots({
575	      workers: scopedWorkers,
576	      runs: records.allRuns,
577	    }),
578	    undefined,
579	    options,
580	    workerEntrySeqs,
581	  );
582	  probe?.mark("buildPayload");
583	  return payload;
584	}

586	type EventPayloadCacheEntry = {
587	  version: number;
588	  promise: Promise<EventPayload>;
589	};
590	
591	const cachedPersistedPayloads = new Map<string, EventPayloadCacheEntry>();
592	const cachedRuntimePayloads = new Map<string, EventPayloadCacheEntry>();
593	
594	export function __clearEventPayloadCachesForTests() {
595	  cachedPersistedPayloads.clear();
596	  cachedRuntimePayloads.clear();
597	}
598	
599	function eventPayloadCacheKey(options: EventPayloadOptions = {}) {
600	  return options.selectedRunId?.trim() || "__all__";
601	}
602	
603	function shareInFlightEventPayload(
604	  cache: Map<string, EventPayloadCacheEntry>,
605	  options: EventPayloadOptions,
606	  build: () => Promise<EventPayload>,
607	) {
608	  const key = eventPayloadCacheKey(options);
609	  const version = getEventStreamNotificationVersion();
610	  const existing = cache.get(key);
611	  if (existing?.version === version) {
612	    return existing.promise;
613	  }
614	
615	  const pending = build().catch((error) => {
616	    const cached = cache.get(key);
617	    if (cached?.promise === pending) {
618	      cache.delete(key);
619	    }
620	    throw error;
621	  });
622	  cache.set(key, { version, promise: pending });
623	  pruneEventPayloadCache(cache);
624	  return pending;
625	}
626	
627	function pruneEventPayloadCache(cache: Map<string, EventPayloadCacheEntry>) {
628	  while (cache.size > EVENT_PAYLOAD_CACHE_LIMIT) {
629	    const oldestKey = cache.keys().next().value;
630	    if (!oldestKey) {
631	      return;
632	    }
633	    cache.delete(oldestKey);
634	  }
635	}
636	
637	function buildSharedPersistedEventPayload(options: EventPayloadOptions = {}, probe?: { mark: (label: string) => void }) {
638	  return shareInFlightEventPayload(
639	    cachedPersistedPayloads,
640	    options,
641	    () => buildPersistedEventPayload(options, probe),
642	  );
643	}
644	
645	async function buildRuntimeEnrichedEventPayload(options: EventPayloadOptions = {}, probe?: { mark: (label: string) => void }) {
646	  let records = await readPersistedEventRecords(options, probe);
647	  probe?.mark("readRecords#1.total");
648	  let scopedWorkers = selectedRunWorkers(records, options);
649	  let workerEntrySeqs = await buildWorkerEntrySeqs(scopedWorkers);
650	  probe?.mark(`workerSeqs#1[${scopedWorkers.length}]`);
651	  let agentsData = buildLiveWorkerSnapshots({
652	    workers: scopedWorkers,
653	    runs: records.allRuns,
654	  });
655	  const frontendErrors: AppErrorPayload[] = [];
656	
657	  try {
658	    const res = await fetchWithTimeout(`${BRIDGE_URL}/agents`, RUNTIME_AGENT_TIMEOUT_MS);
659	    probe?.mark("bridge.fetch");
660	    if (res.ok) {
661	      const rawAgentsPayload = await res.json();
662	      const rawAgents = Array.isArray(rawAgentsPayload) ? rawAgentsPayload : [];
663	      const { syncConversationSessions } = await import("@/server/conversations/sync");
664	      await syncConversationSessions(rawAgents, {
665	        selectedRunId: options.selectedRunId,
666	        refreshPlanningArtifacts: false,
667	      });
668	      probe?.mark("bridge.sync");
669	      // Second reconciliation pass — this one knows what's actually in
670	      // the bridge, so it can detect workers that were "working" when
671	      // the bridge died and are now stranded with no live agent. The
672	      // earlier pass (inside readPersistedEventRecords) couldn't see
673	      // this because it ran before we fetched the bridge agent list.
674	      const bridgeAgentNames = new Set<string>();
675	      for (const agent of rawAgents) {
676	        if (typeof agent === "object" && agent !== null) {
677	          const name = (agent as { name?: unknown }).name;
678	          if (typeof name === "string" && name.length > 0) {
679	            bridgeAgentNames.add(name);
680	          }
681	        }
682	      }
683	      await reconcilePersistedReloadZombies({
684	        selectedRunId: options.selectedRunId,
685	        source: "events-snapshot-post-bridge",
686	        bridgeAgentNames,
687	      });
688	      probe?.mark("reconcile.bridge-orphans");
689	      records = await readPersistedEventRecords(options);
690	      probe?.mark("readRecords#2.total");
691	      scopedWorkers = selectedRunWorkers(records, options);
692	      workerEntrySeqs = await buildWorkerEntrySeqs(scopedWorkers);
693	      probe?.mark(`workerSeqs#2[${scopedWorkers.length}]`);
694	      agentsData = buildLiveWorkerSnapshots({
695	        agents: filterRuntimeAgentsForWorkers(rawAgents, scopedWorkers),
696	        workers: scopedWorkers,
697	        runs: records.allRuns,
698	      });
699	    } else {
700	      const bridgeError = new Error(`Agent runtime list request failed with status ${res.status}.`);
701	      agentsData = buildLiveWorkerSnapshots({
702	        workers: scopedWorkers,
703	        runs: records.allRuns,
704	        bridgeError,
705	      });
706	      if (!isTransientSupervisorError(bridgeError)) {
707	        frontendErrors.push(buildAppError(
708	          bridgeError,
709	          {
710	            source: "Agent runtime",
711	            action: "Stream live agent state",
712	          },
713	        ));
714	      }
715	    }
716	  } catch (error) {
717	    agentsData = buildLiveWorkerSnapshots({
718	      workers: scopedWorkers,
719	      runs: records.allRuns,
720	      bridgeError: error,
721	    });
722	    if (!isTransientSupervisorError(error)) {
723	      frontendErrors.push(buildAppError(error, {
724	        source: "Agent runtime",
725	        action: "Stream live agent state",
726	      }));
727	    }
728	  }
729	
730	  return buildEventPayload(records, agentsData, frontendErrors, options, workerEntrySeqs);
731	}

733	function buildSharedRuntimeEnrichedEventPayload(options: EventPayloadOptions = {}, probe?: { mark: (label: string) => void }) {
734	  return shareInFlightEventPayload(
735	    cachedRuntimePayloads,
736	    options,
737	    () => buildRuntimeEnrichedEventPayload(options, probe),
738	  );
739	}

741	function delay(ms: number) {
742	  return new Promise<void>((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));
743	}
744	
745	function parseLastEventId(raw: string | null | undefined): number | string | null {
746	  if (!raw) {
747	    return null;
748	  }
749	  const trimmed = raw.trim();
750	  if (!trimmed) {
751	    return null;
752	  }
753	  if (parseEventStreamId(trimmed)) {
754	    return trimmed;
755	  }
756	  if (/^\d+$/.test(trimmed)) {
757	    const parsed = Number(trimmed);
758	    return Number.isSafeInteger(parsed) ? parsed : null;
759	  }
760	  return null;
761	}
762	
763	export const handleEventsRequest: OmniHttpHandler = async (request, context) => {
764	  const url = new URL(request.url);
765	  const isSnapshot = url.searchParams.get("snapshot") === "1";
766	  const persistedOnly = url.searchParams.get("persisted") === "1";
767	  const probe = isSnapshot
768	    ? startSlowProbe(`GET /api/events?snapshot=1${persistedOnly ? "&persisted=1" : ""}${url.searchParams.get("runId") ? `&runId=${url.searchParams.get("runId")}` : ""}`)
769	    : null;
770	  const ticketAuth = isSnapshot
771	    ? null
772	    : await redeemStreamTicketRequest(request, "/api/events");
773	  if (ticketAuth?.response) {
774	    probe?.end();
775	    return ticketAuth.response;
776	  }
777	  const auth = ticketAuth
778	    ? { session: null, response: null }
779	    : await requireApiSession(request, {
780	      source: "Events",
781	      action: "Stream live updates",
782	    });
783	  probe?.mark("auth");
784	  if (auth.response) {
785	    probe?.end();
786	    return auth.response;
787	  }
788	
789	  const eventPayloadOptions = {
790	    selectedRunId: url.searchParams.get("runId"),
791	  } satisfies EventPayloadOptions;
792	
793	  if (isSnapshot) {
794	    const payload = persistedOnly
795	      // `persisted=1` is the canonical verification surface used after
796	      // lifecycle mutations. It must reflect SQLite now, even when a route
797	      // bundle did not share the in-process notification version.
798	      ? await buildPersistedEventPayload(eventPayloadOptions, probe ?? undefined)
799	      : await (async () => {
800	        const { ensureSupervisorRuntimeStarted } = await import("@/server/supervisor/runtime-watchdog");
801	        await ensureSupervisorRuntimeStarted();
802	        probe?.mark("ensureSupervisor");
803	        return buildSharedRuntimeEnrichedEventPayload(eventPayloadOptions, probe ?? undefined);
804	      })();
805	    probe?.mark("payload.total");
806	    const requestedChecksum = url.searchParams.get("checksum")?.trim() || "";
807	
808	    // Anchor the snapshot to the current cursor so a subsequent SSE
809	    // connection can pass `Last-Event-ID: <lastEventId>` (or
810	    // `?lastEventId=`) and receive only events newer than this body.
811	    // Exposed as a response header to avoid changing the JSON shape
812	    // that the UI consumes.
813	    const response = Response.json(
814	      requestedChecksum && requestedChecksum === payload.snapshotChecksum
815	        ? {
816	          notModified: true,
817	          snapshotChecksum: payload.snapshotChecksum,
818	          workerEntrySeqs: payload.workerEntrySeqs,
819	        }
820	        : payload,
821	    );
822	    response.headers.set("x-omni-last-event-id", getEventStreamCursor());
823	    if (payload.snapshotChecksum) {
824	      response.headers.set("x-omni-snapshot-checksum", payload.snapshotChecksum);
825	    }
826	    probe?.end();
827	    return response;
828	  }
829	
830	  const { ensureSupervisorRuntimeStarted } = await import("@/server/supervisor/runtime-watchdog");
831	  await ensureSupervisorRuntimeStarted();
832	
833	  const lastEventIdHeader = request.headers.get("last-event-id");
834	  const resumeFromHeader = parseLastEventId(lastEventIdHeader);
835	  const hasCursorQuery = url.searchParams.has("cursor");
836	  const resumeFromCursorQuery = parseLastEventId(url.searchParams.get("cursor"));
837	  const resumeFromLegacyQuery = parseLastEventId(url.searchParams.get("lastEventId"));
838	  const resumeFromId = hasCursorQuery
839	    ? resumeFromCursorQuery
840	    : resumeFromHeader ?? resumeFromLegacyQuery;
841	  const runIdScope = eventPayloadOptions.selectedRunId ?? null;
```

```text
395	function inferWorkerIdFromMessage(message: MessageRecord) {
396	  if (message.workerId?.trim()) {
397	    return message.workerId.trim();
398	  }
399	
400	  const promptedMatch = message.content.match(/^Prompted\s+([^\s:]+):/);
401	  return promptedMatch?.[1] ?? null;
402	}

404	function renderSupervisorActivityText(text: string) {
405	  const match = text.match(/^(Starting (?:worker \d+|planning agent)|Steering worker \d+)([\s\S]*)$/);
406	  if (!match) {
407	    return text;
408	  }
409	
410	  return (
411	    <>
412	      <strong className="font-semibold text-foreground">{match[1]}</strong>
413	      {match[2]}
414	    </>
415	  );
416	}

418	function renderSupervisorActivityIcon(item: Extract<ConversationTimelineItem, { type: "activity" }>) {
419	  const eventType = item.event?.eventType;
420	  const text = item.text.trim();
421	
422	  if (eventType === "worker_spawned" || item.id.startsWith("worker-start:") || text.startsWith("Starting worker ") || text.startsWith("Starting planning agent")) {
423	    return <CirclePlay className="h-3.5 w-3.5" aria-hidden="true" strokeWidth={1.8} />;
424	  }
425	
426	  if (
427	    eventType === "worker_cancelled"
428	    || eventType === "worker_stopped"
429	    || eventType === "worker_stop_requested"
430	    || text.startsWith("Cancelled worker ")
431	    || text.startsWith("Stopped worker ")
432	    || text.startsWith("Stopping worker ")
433	  ) {
434	    return <CircleStop className="h-3.5 w-3.5" aria-hidden="true" strokeWidth={1.8} />;
435	  }
436	
437	  if (
438	    eventType === "worker_prompt_deferred"
439	    || text.startsWith("Steering worker ")
440	    || text.startsWith("Waiting to steer worker ")
441	  ) {
442	    return <Route className="h-3.5 w-3.5" aria-hidden="true" strokeWidth={1.8} />;
443	  }
444	
445	  if (
446	    eventType === "worker_failover_started"
447	    || eventType === "worker_failover_completed"
448	    || eventType === "worker_handoff_emitted"
449	  ) {
450	    return <ArrowLeftRight className="h-3.5 w-3.5" aria-hidden="true" strokeWidth={1.8} />;
451	  }
452	
453	  return null;
454	}

694	function FailoverChip({ events }: { events: ExecutionEventRecord[] }) {
695	  for (let i = events.length - 1; i >= 0; i -= 1) {
696	    const event = events[i]!;
697	    if (event.eventType !== "worker_failover_completed") continue;
698	    let outgoingType: string | null = null;
699	    let newType: string | null = null;
700	    try {
701	      const details = event.details ? JSON.parse(event.details) : null;
702	      if (details && typeof details === "object") {
703	        const record = details as Record<string, unknown>;
704	        outgoingType = typeof record.outgoingType === "string" ? record.outgoingType : null;
705	        newType = typeof record.newType === "string" ? record.newType : null;
706	      }
707	    } catch {
708	      outgoingType = null;
709	      newType = null;
710	    }
711	    if (!outgoingType || !newType) return null;
712	    const outgoingLabel = WORKER_TYPE_LABELS[outgoingType as SupportedWorkerType] ?? outgoingType;
713	    const newLabel = WORKER_TYPE_LABELS[newType as SupportedWorkerType] ?? newType;
714	    return (
715	      <div className="flex">
716	        <span
717	          className="inline-flex items-center gap-1.5 rounded-full border border-amber-200/40 bg-amber-100/30 px-3 py-1 text-xs text-amber-900 dark:border-amber-900/40 dark:bg-amber-950/30 dark:text-amber-200"
718	          aria-label={t("conversation.chip.switchedWorkersAria")}
719	        >
720	          <ArrowLeftRight className="h-3 w-3" aria-hidden="true" strokeWidth={1.8} />
721	          {t("conversation.chip.switchedWorkers", { outgoing: outgoingLabel, incoming: newLabel })}
722	        </span>
723	      </div>
724	    );
725	  }
726	  return null;
727	}

777	export function ConversationMain({
778	  scrollRef,
779	  selectedRunId,
780	  selectedRun,
781	  welcomeRepoName,
782	  isDirectConversation,
783	  isPlanningConversation,
784	  isImplementationConversation,
785	  appErrors,
786	  conversationFailure,
787	  directConversationMessages,
788	  locallySentUserMessageIds,
789	  sendingUserMessageIds,
790	  expandedDirectMessageIds,
791	  toggleDirectMessageExpansion,
792	  primaryConversationAgent,
793	  primaryConversationWorkerId,
794	  initialWorkerEntries = {},
795	  unifiedWorkerStreamEnabled,
796	  isHydratingConversations,
797	  isSelectedConversationPreviewAvailable,
798	  isSelectedConversationLoaded,
799	  promotePlanningConversation,
800	  onStartReview,
801	  reviewRuns = [],
802	  reviewRounds = [],
803	  reviewFindings = [],
804	  conversationTimelineItems,
805	  recoverRun,
806	  recoveryState,
807	  recoveryIncidents,
808	  resumeRunRecovery,
809	  stopRunRecovery,
810	  showRecoverableRunningState,
811	  hasStuckWorker,
812	  latestUserCheckpoint,
813	  handleRetryMessage,
814	  handleResumeRunRecovery,
815	  handleStopRecoveryWait,
816	  handleStartEditingMessage,
817	  handleForkMessage,
818	  handleForkMessageIntoWorktree,
819	  handleConfirmForkMessageIntoWorktree,
820	  editingMessageId,
821	  editingMessageValue,
822	  setEditingMessageValue,
823	  handleCancelEditingMessage,
824	  handleSaveEditedMessage,
825	  handlePreflightConfirmationAnswer,
826	  isPreflightConfirmationAnswering,
827	  conversationAgents,
828	  showDirectControlWorkingIndicator,
829	  directControlPendingAssistantStatus,
830	  showConversationExecution,
831	  liveExecutionStatus,
832	  liveThoughts,
833	  executionEvents,
834	  activeWorkers,
835	  emptyComposer,
836	  projectRoot,
837	  onOpenProjectFile,
838	  onOpenWorkerActivity,
839	  onRespondElicitation,
840	  onRespondPermission,
841	  respondingElicitationRequestId = null,
842	  respondingPermissionRequestId = null,
843	}: ConversationMainProps) {
844	  useI18nSnapshot();
845	  const { hasOutputBelow } = useManagerSnapshot(conversationMainManager);
846	  const { handledMessageIds: handledPreflightConfirmationMessageIds } = useManagerSnapshot(preflightConfirmationActionsManager);
847	  const selectedRunIsTerminal = isTerminalRunStatus(selectedRun?.status);
848	  // Subscribe to the unified worker conversation stream for the
849	  // direct-control worker. When the flag is enabled this drives the
850	  // Terminal directly; otherwise the legacy `agent` + `userMessages`
851	  // path renders. `null` workerId returns an empty state and skips
852	  // the fetch.
853	  const directWorkerStream = useWorkerStream(
854	    unifiedWorkerStreamEnabled ? primaryConversationWorkerId : null,
855	    primaryConversationWorkerId ? initialWorkerEntries[primaryConversationWorkerId] ?? [] : [],
856	    {
857	      refreshIntervalMs: resolveDirectWorkerStreamRefreshInterval({
858	        unifiedWorkerStreamEnabled,
859	        primaryConversationWorkerId,
860	        activeRefreshIntervalMs: DIRECT_WORKER_STREAM_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS,
861	        validationIntervalMs: DIRECT_WORKER_STREAM_VALIDATION_INTERVAL_MS,
862	        showDirectControlWorkingIndicator,
863	        selectedRunIsTerminal,
864	      }),
865	    },
866	  );
867	  // The single-worker stream above is only the *active* worker's
868	  // transcript. When a run has cycled through multiple workers
869	  // (cancel → respawn) we also fetch the merged conversation
870	  // transcript so prior workers' content stays visible. The merged
871	  // stream is preferred when available; we fall back to the active
872	  // worker stream during the brief moment before the transcript hook
873	  // produces its first response.
874	  const conversationTranscript = useConversationTranscript(
875	    unifiedWorkerStreamEnabled ? selectedRunId : null,
876	    {
877	      enabled: unifiedWorkerStreamEnabled && Boolean(selectedRunId),
878	      refreshIntervalMs: resolveDirectWorkerStreamRefreshInterval({
```

```text
11	import { useCallback, useEffect, useMemo, useSyncExternalStore } from "react";

17	export interface ConversationTranscriptEntry extends WorkerEntry {
18	  workerId: string;
19	}

21	export interface ConversationTranscriptState {
22	  entries: ConversationTranscriptEntry[];
23	  latestToken: string | null;
24	  oldestToken: string | null;

31	   * `status` cycles back through "loading" on every poll refresh, so
32	   * render gates must use this instead of `status === "loaded"`.

58	export const EMPTY_CONVERSATION_TRANSCRIPT_STATE = EMPTY;

60	export interface ConversationTranscriptManagerOptions {
61	  transcript?: RuntimeAPIs["conversations"]["transcript"];
62	}
63	
64	export class ConversationTranscriptManager {
65	  private readonly stateByRunId = new Map<string, ConversationTranscriptState>();
66	  private readonly listenersByRunId = new Map<string, Set<() => void>>();
67	  private readonly inFlightByRunId = new Map<string, Promise<void>>();
68	  private transcript: RuntimeAPIs["conversations"]["transcript"] | null;
69	
70	  constructor(options: ConversationTranscriptManagerOptions = {}) {
71	    this.transcript = options.transcript ?? null;

78	  private load(input: Parameters<RuntimeAPIs["conversations"]["transcript"]>[0]) {
79	    if (!this.transcript) {

81	    }
82	    return this.transcript(input) as Promise<TranscriptFetchResponse>;
83	  }
84	
85	  getState(runId: string): ConversationTranscriptState {
86	    return this.stateByRunId.get(runId) ?? EMPTY;
87	  }
88	
89	  subscribe(runId: string, listener: () => void): () => void {
90	    const listeners = this.listenersByRunId.get(runId) ?? new Set();
91	    listeners.add(listener);
92	    this.listenersByRunId.set(runId, listeners);
93	    return () => {
94	      const current = this.listenersByRunId.get(runId);
95	      if (!current) return;
96	      current.delete(listener);
97	      if (current.size === 0) {

147	    const previous = this.getState(runId);
148	    this.updateState(runId, { ...previous, status: "loading", lastError: null });
149	    const promise = this.load({ runId, limit }).then(
150	      (response) => {
151	        const current = this.getState(runId);
152	        const next: ConversationTranscriptState = {
153	          ...current,
154	          entries: coalesceWorkerEntriesById(response.entries) as ConversationTranscriptEntry[],
155	          latestToken: response.latestToken,
156	          oldestToken: response.oldestToken ?? null,
157	          hasOlder: Boolean(response.hasOlder),
158	          workerIds: response.workerIds,
159	          status: "loaded",
160	          lastError: null,
161	          hasLoadedOnce: true,
162	        };
163	        this.updateState(runId, next);
164	      },
165	      (error: unknown) => {
166	        const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
167	        const failing = this.getState(runId);
168	        this.updateState(runId, { ...failing, status: "error", lastError: message });
169	      },
170	    ).finally(() => {
171	      this.inFlightByRunId.delete(runId);
172	    });
173	    this.inFlightByRunId.set(runId, promise);
174	    return promise;
175	  }
176	
177	  private async fetchForward(runId: string, latestToken: string): Promise<void> {
178	    const previous = this.getState(runId);
179	    this.updateState(runId, { ...previous, status: "loading", lastError: null });
180	    const promise = this.load({ runId, afterToken: latestToken }).then(
181	      (response) => {
182	        const current = this.getState(runId);
183	        const next: ConversationTranscriptState = {
184	          ...current,
185	          entries: coalesceWorkerEntriesById([...current.entries, ...response.entries]) as ConversationTranscriptEntry[],
186	          latestToken: response.latestToken,
187	          oldestToken: current.oldestToken ?? response.oldestToken ?? null,
188	          hasOlder: current.hasOlder || Boolean(response.hasOlder),
189	          workerIds: response.workerIds,
190	          status: "loaded",
191	          lastError: null,
192	          hasLoadedOnce: true,
193	        };
194	        this.updateState(runId, next);

208	  private async fetchOlder(runId: string, oldestToken: string, limit: number): Promise<void> {
209	    const previous = this.getState(runId);
```
