```text
export async function reconcileOrphanedProcessSessions() {
  if (reconcileStarted) {
    return;
  }
  reconcileStarted = true;
  const rows = await db.select().from(processSessions).where(inArray(processSessions.status, ["starting", "running"]));
  for (const row of rows) {
    if (liveProcesses.has(row.runId)) {
      continue;
    }
    await appendSessionLifecycleEntry({
      runId: row.runId,
      workerId: row.workerId,
      text: "Process session was orphaned after server restart.",
      raw: { eventType: "process.orphaned_after_restart" },
    });
    await setProcessStatus({
      runId: row.runId,
      workerId: row.workerId,
      prev: row.status,
      next: "orphaned",
      reason: "server_restart",
      lastError: "Process session was orphaned after server restart.",
    });
    emitNamedEvent({
      kind: "error.surfaced",
      code: "process.orphaned_after_restart",
      message: "A running process session was orphaned after the server restarted.",
      surface: "banner",
      runId: row.runId,
      workerId: row.workerId,
    });
  }
}

import { asc, eq } from "drizzle-orm";
import path from "path";
import { db } from "@/server/db";
import { runs, workers } from "@/server/db/schema";
import { emitNamedEvent } from "@/server/events/named-events";
import { openRecoveryIncident, markRecoveryIncidentNeedsUser } from "@/server/runs/recovery-incidents";
import { setRunNeedsRecovery } from "@/server/runs/recovery-actions";
import { isTerminalRunStatus, normalizeRunStatus } from "@/server/runs/status";
import { resumeMissingDirectWorker } from "@/server/conversations/send-message";
import { notifyEventStreamSubscribers } from "@/server/events/live-updates";
import { readWorkerSessionMetadata } from "@/server/workers/session-metadata";

const STARTING_WORKER_RELOAD_GRACE_MS = 30_000;
const ACTIVE_WORKER_RELOAD_GRACE_MS = 15_000;
const LOST_WORKER_REASON = "Worker was marked active but is not present in the bridge runtime.";

function normalizedWorkerStatus(worker: typeof workers.$inferSelect) {
  return normalizeRunStatus(worker.status).split(":")[0]?.trim() ?? "";
}

function isPastGrace(worker: typeof workers.$inferSelect, nowMs: number) {
  const status = normalizedWorkerStatus(worker);
  const graceMs = status === "starting"
    ? STARTING_WORKER_RELOAD_GRACE_MS
    : ACTIVE_WORKER_RELOAD_GRACE_MS;
  return nowMs - worker.updatedAt.getTime() >= graceMs;
}

function isPathInside(root: string, candidate: string) {
  const relative = path.relative(root, candidate);
  return relative === "" || (!relative.startsWith("..") && !path.isAbsolute(relative));
}

function workerMatchesRunProject(run: typeof runs.$inferSelect, worker: typeof workers.$inferSelect) {
  if (!run.projectPath?.trim()) {
    return true;
  }
  const projectPath = path.resolve(run.projectPath);
  const workerCwd = path.resolve(worker.cwd);
  return isPathInside(projectPath, workerCwd);
}

function isRunEligible(status: string | null | undefined) {
  const normalized = normalizeRunStatus(status);
  return Boolean(normalized)
    && !isTerminalRunStatus(normalized)
    && normalized !== "awaiting_user"
    && normalized !== "needs_recovery"
    && normalized !== "recovering"
    && normalized !== "quota_waiting";
}

function isStaleStartingWorker(worker: typeof workers.$inferSelect, nowMs: number) {
  if (normalizedWorkerStatus(worker) !== "starting") {
    return false;
  }
  if (worker.bridgeSessionId?.trim()) {
    return false;
  }
  return isPastGrace(worker, nowMs);
}

// Workers that were actively producing output when the bridge died:
// `status="working"` in the DB but absent from the bridge's live agent
// list. Without this, the FE shows "running" in the sidebar and no
// "Thinking…" indicator forever, because the DB row never advances and
// the bridge has no agent to report state for. We auto-resume via the
// same spawn-with-saved-session path that the regular send-message
// flow uses.
function isOrphanedActiveWorker(
  worker: typeof workers.$inferSelect,
  bridgeAgentNames: ReadonlySet<string>,
  nowMs: number,
): boolean {
  const status = normalizedWorkerStatus(worker);
  if (status !== "starting" && status !== "working" && status !== "stuck" && status !== "recovering") {
    return false;
  }
  // The bridge knows about it — nothing for us to do.
  if (bridgeAgentNames.has(worker.id)) {
    return false;
  }
  return isPastGrace(worker, nowMs);
}

async function markWorkerLost(worker: typeof workers.$inferSelect) {
  if (normalizedWorkerStatus(worker) === "lost") {
    return;
  }
  await db.update(workers).set({
    status: "lost",
    currentText: "",
    updatedAt: new Date(),
  }).where(eq(workers.id, worker.id));
  emitNamedEvent({
    kind: "worker.status",
    runId: worker.runId,
    workerId: worker.id,
    prev: worker.status,
    next: "lost",
  });
}

async function markStaleWorkerNeedsUser(args: {
  run: typeof runs.$inferSelect;
  worker: typeof workers.$inferSelect;
  source?: string;
  reason: string;
  autoRecoveryError?: string | null;
}) {
  await markWorkerLost(args.worker);
  await setRunNeedsRecovery({
    runId: args.run.id,
    reason: args.reason,
  });
  const incident = await openRecoveryIncident({
    runId: args.run.id,
    workerId: args.worker.id,
    queuedMessageId: null,
    kind: "worker_lost",
```

```text
23	  const incomingItems = incoming ?? [];

63	  const merged: Record<string, string> = {};
64	
65	  for (const [runId, readAt] of Object.entries(current.readMarkers ?? {})) {

68	    }

70	
71	  for (const [runId, readAt] of Object.entries(incoming.readMarkers ?? {})) {

83	function mergeScopedCatalog(current: EventStreamState, incoming: EventStreamState) {

108	  serverAuthoritative: boolean;

145	function mergeScopedMessages(current: EventStreamState, incoming: EventStreamState) {
146	  const incomingMessages = incoming.messages ?? [];

225	function mergeScopedCachedState(current: EventStreamState, cached: EventStreamState): EventStreamState {
226	  // hydrateFromCacheScope swaps scopes (e.g. on session switch). The cached

258	/**

270	  private readonly snapshotCache: EventStreamSnapshotCacheManager;

272	
273	  constructor(initialState: EventStreamState, options: {

312	
313	  hydrateFromCacheScope(scope: string | null | undefined) {
314	    this.snapshotCacheScope = scope?.trim() || null;
315	    if (authoritativeCatalogExcludesScope(this.state, this.snapshotCacheScope)) {
316	      return false;
317	    }
318	    if (
319	      this.state.snapshotSource === "server"
320	      && this.snapshotCacheScope
```

```text
import {
  type AppErrorDescriptor,
  normalizeAppError,
} from "@/lib/app-errors";
import { compareEventStreamIds, parseEventStreamId } from "@/shared/runtime";
import type { RuntimeAPIs, RuntimeSubscription } from "@/runtime-api/types";
import {
  buildEventStreamUrl,
  createLegacyLiveEventAPIs,
} from "@/runtime-api/legacy-live-events";
import type { EventStreamState } from "./types";
import { workerEntriesManager } from "./WorkerEntriesManager";
import { sidebarWorkerActivityManager, type SidebarWorkerActivityManager } from "./SidebarWorkerActivityManager";

export { buildEventStreamUrl };

const SNAPSHOT_FALLBACK_INTERVAL_MS = 15_000;
const SNAPSHOT_FALLBACK_COOLDOWN_MS = 1_000;
const SNAPSHOT_VALIDATION_INTERVAL_MS = 5_000;

interface LiveEventConnectionManagerOptions {
  selectedRunId?: string | null;
  initialLastEventId?: string | number | null;
  cursor?: LiveEventCursorManager;
  events?: Pick<RuntimeAPIs["events"], "snapshot" | "open">;
  /** @deprecated Test-only compatibility. Production injects RuntimeAPIs.events. */
  EventSourceConstructor?: typeof EventSource;
  /** @deprecated Test-only compatibility. Production injects RuntimeAPIs.events. */
  requestJson?: <T>(
    input: RequestInfo | URL,
    init?: RequestInit,
    fallback?: Partial<AppErrorDescriptor>,
  ) => Promise<T>;
  /** @deprecated Test-only compatibility. Production injects RuntimeAPIs.events. */
  requestSnapshot?: (
    input: RequestInfo | URL,
    init: RequestInit | undefined,
    fallback: Partial<AppErrorDescriptor>,
  ) => Promise<SnapshotPollResult>;
  getSnapshotChecksum?: () => string | null | undefined;
  workerEntries?: Pick<typeof workerEntriesManager, "onKnownSeqs" | "onStreamResync" | "onWakeUp">;
  sidebarWorkerActivity?: Pick<SidebarWorkerActivityManager, "onKnownSeqs" | "onWakeUp">;
  applyUpdate: (state: EventStreamState) => void;
  reportError: (error: AppErrorDescriptor) => void;
  onStreamResync?: () => void;
  fallbackIntervalMs?: number;
  fallbackCooldownMs?: number;
  snapshotValidationIntervalMs?: number | null;
}

type SnapshotPollResponse = EventStreamState | {
  notModified: true;
  snapshotChecksum?: string;
  workerEntrySeqs?: Record<string, number>;
};

interface SnapshotPollResult {
  data: SnapshotPollResponse;
  lastEventId?: string | null;
}

function withFallbackErrorContext(
  error: unknown,
  fallback: Pick<AppErrorDescriptor, "source" | "action">,
) {
  const normalized = normalizeAppError(error, fallback);
  return {
    ...normalized,
    source: normalized.source || fallback.source,
    action: normalized.action || fallback.action,
  };
}

function isTransientConnectivityError(error: unknown) {
  if (!(error instanceof Error)) {
    return false;
  }

  if (error.name === "AbortError" || error.name === "NetworkError") {
    return true;
  }

  if (!(error instanceof TypeError)) {
    return false;
  }

  const message = error.message.toLowerCase();
  return (
    message.includes("failed to fetch")
    || message.includes("network")
    || message.includes("load failed")
    || message.includes("offline")
  );
}

function normalizeLastEventId(lastEventId: string | number | null | undefined) {
  const value = String(lastEventId ?? "").trim();
  return value || null;
}

function compareEventIds(left: string, right: string) {
  if (parseEventStreamId(left) && parseEventStreamId(right)) {
    return compareEventStreamIds(left, right);
  }
  if (/^\d+$/.test(left) && /^\d+$/.test(right)) {
    const leftValue = BigInt(left);
    const rightValue = BigInt(right);
    return leftValue === rightValue ? 0 : leftValue > rightValue ? 1 : -1;
  }
  return left === right ? 0 : null;
}

export class LiveEventCursorManager {
  private lastEventId: string | null = null;
  private readonly storage: Pick<Storage, "getItem" | "setItem" | "removeItem"> | null;
  private readonly storageKey: string | null;

  constructor(
    initialLastEventId?: string | number | null,
    options: {
      scopeKey?: string | null;
      storage?: Pick<Storage, "getItem" | "setItem" | "removeItem"> | null;
    } = {},
  ) {
    this.storage = options.storage ?? null;
    const scopeKey = options.scopeKey?.trim() ?? "";
    this.storageKey = scopeKey
      ? `omniharness:event-cursor:${scopeKey}`
      : null;
    if (this.storage && this.storageKey) {
      this.advance(this.storage.getItem(this.storageKey));
    }
    this.advance(initialLastEventId);
  }

  getCurrent() {
    return this.lastEventId;
  }

  advance(lastEventId: string | number | null | undefined) {
    const normalized = normalizeLastEventId(lastEventId);
    if (!normalized) return false;
    if (this.lastEventId) {
      const ordering = compareEventIds(normalized, this.lastEventId);
      if (ordering !== null && ordering <= 0) {
        return false;
      }
    }
    this.lastEventId = normalized;
    if (this.storage && this.storageKey) {
      this.storage.setItem(this.storageKey, normalized);
    }
    return true;
  }

  clear() {
    this.lastEventId = null;
    if (this.storage && this.storageKey) {
      this.storage.removeItem(this.storageKey);
    }
  }
}

function isNotModifiedSnapshot(value: SnapshotPollResponse): value is Extract<SnapshotPollResponse, { notModified: true }> {
  return typeof value === "object" && value !== null && "notModified" in value && value.notModified === true;
}
```

```text
function hasNearbyMirroredMessage(event: ExecutionEventRecord, messages: MessageRecord[]) {
  if (!MESSAGE_MIRRORED_CONVERSATION_TIMELINE_EVENT_TYPES.has(event.eventType)) {
    return false;
  }

  const eventTime = timestampMs(event.createdAt);
  return messages.some((message) => (
    message.runId === event.runId
    && (message.kind === "supervisor_action" || message.kind === "clarification" || message.kind === "completion")
    && Math.abs(timestampMs(message.createdAt) - eventTime) <= 2_000
  ));
}

function shouldShowExecutionEventInTimeline(event: ExecutionEventRecord, messages: MessageRecord[]) {
  if (classifyExecutionEvent(event) !== "inline_event") {
    return false;
  }

  return !hasNearbyMirroredMessage(event, messages);
}

export function buildConversationTimelineItems({
  messages,
  executionEvents,
  supervisorInterventions = [],
  workers = [],
  isPlanningRun = false,
}: {
  messages: MessageRecord[];
  executionEvents: ExecutionEventRecord[];
  supervisorInterventions?: SupervisorInterventionRecord[];
  workers?: ConversationWorkerRecord[];
  isPlanningRun?: boolean;
}): ConversationTimelineItem[] {
  const items: ConversationTimelineItem[] = messages
    .filter(shouldRenderMessageInMainConversation)
    .map((message) => ({
      type: "message",
      id: message.id,
      createdAt: message.createdAt,
      message,
    }));
  const sortedExecutionEvents = [...executionEvents].sort((a, b) => {
    const timeDelta = timestampMs(a.createdAt) - timestampMs(b.createdAt);
    return timeDelta !== 0 ? timeDelta : a.id.localeCompare(b.id);
  });
  const workerIdsWithSpawnEvents = new Set(
    executionEvents
      .filter((event) => event.eventType === "worker_spawned" && event.workerId)
      .map((event) => event.workerId as string),
  );

  for (const worker of workers) {
    if (!worker.createdAt || workerIdsWithSpawnEvents.has(worker.id)) {
      continue;
    }

    items.push({
      type: "activity",
      id: `worker-start:${worker.id}`,
      createdAt: worker.createdAt,
      text: summarizeWorkerStartRecord(worker, isPlanningRun),
    });
  }

  for (const event of sortedExecutionEvents) {
    if (!shouldShowExecutionEventInTimeline(event, messages)) {
      continue;
    }

    const text = (event.eventType === "worker_spawned"
      ? summarizeWorkerSpawnEvent(event, isPlanningRun)
      : summarizeInlineEvent(event))?.trim() ?? "";
    if (!text) {
      continue;
    }

    items.push({
      type: "activity",
      id: event.id,
      createdAt: event.createdAt,
      event,
      text,
    });
  }

  for (const intervention of supervisorInterventions) {
    const text = summarizeSupervisorIntervention(intervention);
    if (!text) {
      continue;
    }

    items.push({
      type: "activity",
      id: intervention.id,
      createdAt: intervention.createdAt,
      text,
    });
  }

  return items.sort((a, b) => {
    const timeDelta = timestampMs(a.createdAt) - timestampMs(b.createdAt);
    if (timeDelta !== 0) {
      return timeDelta;
    }
    if (a.type !== b.type) {
      return a.type === "message" ? -1 : 1;
    }
    return a.id.localeCompare(b.id);
  });
}
```

```text
  const text = value ?? "";

) {
```

```text
3	import { useRef } from "react";

5	
6	// The Recent ("Active") tab lists conversations sorted by latest activity. That
7	// membership and sort are recomputed on every event-stream update, so while the
8	// user watches the tab rows can disappear, appear, or reshuffle on every turn.
9	// This hook freezes the row/group membership and order captured at the moment
10	// the tab becomes active, then overlays any still-present live row data so
11	// statuses and unread indicators can update without changing the list itself.
12	// Leaving the tab and returning re-snapshots the list.
13	
14	type SnapshottedRun = SidebarGroup["runs"][number];
15	
16	type SnapshottedGroup = {
17	  group: SidebarGroup;
18	  runOrder: string[];
19	  runsById: Map<string, SnapshottedRun>;
20	};
21	
22	type OrderSnapshot = {
23	  groupOrder: string[];
24	  groupsByPath: Map<string, SnapshottedGroup>;
25	};
26	
27	function captureOrder(groups: SidebarGroup[]): OrderSnapshot {
28	  const groupOrder: string[] = [];
29	  const groupsByPath = new Map<string, SnapshottedGroup>();
30	
31	  groups.forEach((group) => {
32	    groupOrder.push(group.path);
33	    const runOrder = group.runs.map((run) => run.id);
34	    const runsById = new Map(group.runs.map((run) => [run.id, run]));
35	    groupsByPath.set(group.path, {
36	      group: { ...group, runs: [...group.runs] },
37	      runOrder,
38	      runsById,
39	    });
40	  });
41	  return { groupOrder, groupsByPath };
42	}
43	
44	function applyOrder(groups: SidebarGroup[], snapshot: OrderSnapshot, liveCatalogGroups: SidebarGroup[] = groups): SidebarGroup[] {
45	  const liveGroupsByPath = new Map(groups.map((group) => [group.path, group]));
46	  const liveCatalogGroupsByPath = new Map(liveCatalogGroups.map((group) => [group.path, group]));
47	
48	  return snapshot.groupOrder.flatMap((groupPath) => {
49	    const snapshotted = snapshot.groupsByPath.get(groupPath);
50	    if (!snapshotted) return [];
51	
52	    const liveGroup = liveGroupsByPath.get(groupPath);
53	    const liveCatalogGroup = liveCatalogGroupsByPath.get(groupPath);
54	    const liveRunsById = new Map((liveGroup?.runs ?? []).map((run) => [run.id, run]));
55	    const liveCatalogRunsById = new Map((liveCatalogGroup?.runs ?? []).map((run) => [run.id, run]));
56	    const runs = snapshotted.runOrder.flatMap((runId) => {
57	      const run = liveRunsById.get(runId) ?? liveCatalogRunsById.get(runId) ?? snapshotted.runsById.get(runId);
58	      return run ? [run] : [];
59	    });
60	
61	    if (runs.length === 0) return [];
62	
63	    return [{
64	      ...(liveGroup ?? liveCatalogGroup ?? snapshotted.group),
65	      runs,
66	    }];
67	  });
68	}
```

```text
3	import { useCallback, useRef, useSyncExternalStore } from "react";
4	import type { StateManager } from "@/lib/state-manager";

6	export function useManagerSnapshot<TState>(manager: StateManager<TState>) {
7	  return useSyncExternalStore(
8	    useCallback((listener) => manager.subscribe(listener), [manager]),
9	    useCallback(() => manager.getSnapshot(), [manager]),
10	    useCallback(() => manager.getInitialSnapshot(), [manager]),
11	  );
12	}
13	
14	export function shallowEqualRecord<TRecord extends Record<string, unknown>>(
15	  left: TRecord,
16	  right: TRecord,
17	) {
18	  if (Object.is(left, right)) {
19	    return true;
20	  }
21	
22	  const leftKeys = Object.keys(left);
23	  const rightKeys = Object.keys(right);
24	  if (leftKeys.length !== rightKeys.length) {
25	    return false;
26	  }
27	
28	  return leftKeys.every((key) => Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(right, key)
29	    && Object.is(left[key], right[key]));
30	}
31	
32	export function useManagerSelector<TState, TSelected>(
33	  manager: StateManager<TState>,
34	  selector: (state: TState) => TSelected,
35	  isEqual: (left: TSelected, right: TSelected) => boolean = Object.is,
36	) {
37	  const selectionRef = useRef<{
38	    state: TState;
39	    selection: TSelected;
40	  } | null>(null);
41	  const serverSelectionRef = useRef<{
42	    state: TState;
43	    selector: (state: TState) => TSelected;
44	    selection: TSelected;
45	  } | null>(null);
46	
47	  const getSelectedSnapshot = useCallback(() => {
48	    const state = manager.getSnapshot();
49	    const previous = selectionRef.current;
50	    if (previous?.state === state) {
51	      return previous.selection;
52	    }
53	
54	    const nextSelection = selector(state);
55	    if (previous && isEqual(previous.selection, nextSelection)) {
56	      selectionRef.current = {
57	        state,
58	        selection: previous.selection,
59	      };
60	      return previous.selection;
61	    }
62	
63	    selectionRef.current = {
64	      state,
65	      selection: nextSelection,
66	    };
67	    return nextSelection;
68	  }, [isEqual, manager, selector]);
69	  const getServerSelectedSnapshot = useCallback(() => {
70	    const state = manager.getInitialSnapshot();
71	    const previous = serverSelectionRef.current;
72	    if (previous?.state === state && previous.selector === selector) {
73	      return previous.selection;
74	    }
75	    const selection = selector(state);
76	    serverSelectionRef.current = { state, selector, selection };
77	    return selection;
78	  }, [manager, selector]);
79	
80	  return useSyncExternalStore(
81	    useCallback((listener) => manager.subscribe(listener), [manager]),
82	    getSelectedSnapshot,
83	    getServerSelectedSnapshot,
84	  );
85	}
```

```text
function ToolActivity({
  activity,
  variant,
  projectRoot,
  onOpenProjectFile,
}: {
  activity: Extract<AgentActivityItem, { kind: "tool" }>;
  variant: "terminal" | "native";
  projectRoot?: string | null;
  onOpenProjectFile?: (file: ProjectFileReference) => void;
}) {
  const isDone = isTerminalToolStatus(activity.status);
  const showToolLabel = activity.label !== "Tool";
  const { toolDetailsOpenById, toolOutputExpandedById } = useManagerSnapshot(terminalUiManager);
  const detailsOpen = toolDetailsOpenById[activity.id] ?? !isDone;
  const outputIsDiff = activity.outputPane?.kind === "diff";
  const outputExpanded = toolOutputExpandedById[activity.id] ?? outputIsDiff;
  const hasToolPanes = Boolean(activity.inputPane || activity.outputPane);

  return (
    <div className="space-y-1.5">
      <button
        type="button"
        className="group/tool flex w-full flex-wrap items-center gap-1.5 text-left"
        onClick={() => {
          const nextDetailsOpen = !detailsOpen;
          if (nextDetailsOpen && outputIsDiff) {
            terminalUiManager.setToolOutputExpanded(activity.id, true);
          } else if (detailsOpen) {
            terminalUiManager.setToolOutputExpanded(activity.id, false);
          }
          terminalUiManager.setToolDetailsOpen(activity.id, nextDetailsOpen);
        }}
        aria-expanded={detailsOpen}
      >
        {showToolLabel ? (
          <span className={cn("text-[length:var(--terminal-tool-label-size)] font-semibold tracking-tight", variant === "native" ? "text-foreground" : "text-foreground dark:text-zinc-100")}>{activity.label}</span>
        ) : null}
        <span
          className={cn(
            "font-mono leading-[1.45]",
            showToolLabel ? "text-[length:var(--terminal-tool-title-size)]" : "text-[length:var(--terminal-tool-label-size)]",
            variant === "native" ? "text-muted-foreground" : "text-muted-foreground dark:text-zinc-300/95",
          )}
        >
          {activity.title}
        </span>
        {shouldShowToolSpinner(activity.status) ? (
          <LoaderCircle
            className={cn(
              "h-3 w-3 shrink-0 animate-spin",
              variant === "native" ? "text-muted-foreground" : "text-muted-foreground dark:text-zinc-400",
            )}
            aria-label={formatActivityStatus(activity.status)}
          />
        ) : null}
        {shouldShowToolStatusBadge(activity.status) ? (
          <span
            className={cn(
              "rounded-full border px-1.5 py-0.5 font-mono text-[length:var(--terminal-badge-size)] font-semibold uppercase tracking-[0.1em]",
              statusBadgeClass(activity.status, variant),
            )}
          >
            {formatActivityStatus(activity.status)}
          </span>
        ) : null}
        <ChevronDown
          className={cn(
            "h-3 w-3 shrink-0 transition-transform duration-200 ease-out",
            detailsOpen && "rotate-180",
            variant === "native" ? "text-muted-foreground group-hover/tool:text-foreground" : "text-muted-foreground group-hover/tool:text-foreground dark:text-zinc-500 dark:group-hover/tool:text-zinc-200",
          )}
          aria-hidden="true"
        />
      </button>
      {hasToolPanes ? (
        <div
          className={cn(
            TERMINAL_REVEAL_CLASS,
            detailsOpen ? TERMINAL_REVEAL_OPEN_CLASS : TERMINAL_REVEAL_CLOSED_CLASS,
          )}
          aria-hidden={!detailsOpen}
        >
          <div className="min-h-0 overflow-hidden">
            <div className="space-y-1.5 pb-0.5 pt-0.5">
              {activity.inputPane ? (
                <ActivityPane
                  label={activity.inputPane.label}
                  text={activity.inputPane.text}
                  variant={variant}
                  projectRoot={projectRoot}
                  onOpenProjectFile={onOpenProjectFile}
                />
              ) : null}
              {activity.outputPane?.kind === "diff" ? (
                <DiffPane
                  text={activity.outputPane.text}
                  variant={variant}
                  preview
                  expanded={outputExpanded}
                  interactive={detailsOpen}
                  onClick={() => terminalUiManager.setToolOutputExpanded(activity.id, !outputExpanded)}
                />
              ) : activity.outputPane ? (
                <ActivityPane
                  label={activity.outputPane.label}
                  text={activity.outputPane.text}
                  variant={variant}
                  projectRoot={projectRoot}
                  onOpenProjectFile={onOpenProjectFile}
                  preview
                  expanded={outputExpanded}
                  interactive={detailsOpen}
                  onClick={() => terminalUiManager.setToolOutputExpanded(activity.id, !outputExpanded)}
                />
              ) : null}
            </div>
          </div>
        </div>
      ) : null}
    </div>
  );
}
```

```text
export function useWorkerStream(
  workerId: string | null,
  initialEntries: WorkerEntry[] = [],
  options: UseWorkerStreamOptions = {},
) {
  const runtimeApis = useRuntimeAPIs();
  workerEntriesManager.configure(runtimeApis.workers.listEntries);
  const state = useSyncExternalStore(
    useCallback((listener) => (
      workerId ? workerEntriesManager.subscribe(workerId, listener) : () => {}
    ), [workerId]),
    useCallback(() => (
      workerId ? workerEntriesManager.getState(workerId, initialEntries) : EMPTY_WORKER_STREAM_STATE
    ), [initialEntries, workerId]),
    () => EMPTY_WORKER_STREAM_STATE,
  );
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!workerId) {
      return;
    }
    void workerEntriesManager.ensureLoaded(workerId);
  }, [workerId]);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!workerId || !options.refreshIntervalMs || options.refreshIntervalMs <= 0) {
      return;
    }
    const intervalId = window.setInterval(() => {
      void workerEntriesManager.refresh(workerId);
    }, options.refreshIntervalMs);
    return () => window.clearInterval(intervalId);
  }, [options.refreshIntervalMs, workerId]);
  const loadOlder = useCallback((limit?: number) => {
    if (!workerId) return Promise.resolve();
    return workerEntriesManager.loadOlder(workerId, limit);
  }, [workerId]);
  const entries = useMemo(() => coalesceWorkerEntriesById(state.entries), [state.entries]);
  return {
    state,
    entries,
    isLoaded: workerId ? workerEntriesManager.isLoaded(workerId) : false,
    hasEverLoaded: workerId ? workerEntriesManager.hasEverLoaded(workerId) : false,
    hasOlder: state.hasOlder,
    loadOlder,
  };
}
```

```text
export type StateUpdate<T> = T | ((current: T) => T);
export type StateListener = () => void;

export class StateManager<TState> {
  private state: TState;
  private readonly initialState: TState;
  private readonly listeners = new Set<StateListener>();

  constructor(initialState: TState) {
    this.state = initialState;
    this.initialState = initialState;
  }

  getSnapshot() {
    return this.state;
  }

  getInitialSnapshot() {
    return this.initialState;
  }

  subscribe(listener: StateListener) {
    this.listeners.add(listener);
    return () => {
      this.listeners.delete(listener);
    };
  }

  update(updater: StateUpdate<TState>, notify = true) {
    const nextState = typeof updater === "function"
      ? (updater as (current: TState) => TState)(this.state)
      : updater;

    if (Object.is(nextState, this.state)) {
      return this.state;
    }

    this.state = nextState;
    if (notify) {
      this.listeners.forEach((listener) => listener());
    }
    return this.state;
  }

  patch(patch: Partial<TState> | ((current: TState) => Partial<TState>), notify = true) {
    return this.update((current) => ({
      ...current,
      ...(typeof patch === "function" ? patch(current) : patch),
    }), notify);
  }

  setKey<TKey extends keyof TState>(key: TKey, value: StateUpdate<TState[TKey]>, notify = true) {
    return this.update((current) => {
      const nextValue = typeof value === "function"
        ? (value as (currentValue: TState[TKey]) => TState[TKey])(current[key])
        : value;

      if (Object.is(nextValue, current[key])) {
        return current;
      }

      return {
        ...current,
        [key]: nextValue,
      };
    }, notify);
  }
}
```

## Claude subagent agent-a032cc12d75f46e38: Claude · 2026-08-05T10:33:05.607Z

```text
This is the smoking gun. Every worker output entry calls `emitNamedEvent` → `notifyEventStreamSubscribers()`, which wakes the SSE loop to rebuild and push a **full snapshot**.

# SSE Ingestion → React Re-render: Performance Report

## Architecture summary

There is **no delta protocol**. The SSE `update` frame *is* a full `/api/events` snapshot. The client `applyUpdate` path replaces the entire top-level state object, and `HomeApp` subscribes to that single object with no selectors. Every worker output delta from **any** run therefore re-renders the whole app.

---

## Q1: What does one SSE frame invalidate/refetch?

**It does not refetch — it's worse: the server pushes the entire snapshot inline, unthrottled.**

Path for a single worker output delta:

1. `src/server/workers/output-store.ts:1228` / `src/server/workers/stream-writer.ts:99` — each appended worker entry calls `emitNamedEvent({kind: "worker.entry_appended", ...})`.
2. `src/server/events/named-events.ts:739-743` — `emitNamedEvent` unconditionally calls `notifyEventStreamSubscribers()`.
3. `src/server/events/live-updates.ts:9-14` — bumps `notificationVersion` and fires every listener synchronously. **No debounce, no throttle, no coalescing window.**
4. `src/runtime/http/routes/events.ts:1007` — the parked `waitForEventStreamNotification(STREAM_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS=15_000, ...)` resolves *immediately* on notify (`live-updates.ts:22-25` short-circuits if version advanced), breaking the wait loop.
5. `events.ts:968-986` — the loop rebuilds a **full payload** (`buildSharedRuntimeEnrichedEventPayload`), which hits ~17 DB queries (`events.ts:95-191`), a bridge HTTP fetch (`events.ts:658`), and a full `syncConversationSessions` + `reconcilePersistedReloadZombies` pass.
6. `events.ts:912-939` — `sendUpdateIfChanged` `JSON.stringify`s the whole payload, compares to `lastUpdatePayload` (a full string compare of a multi-hundred-KB string), and writes `writeFrame(marker.streamId, "update", serializedPayload)`.

Client-side, `LiveEventConnectionManager.handleUpdateEvent` (`LiveEventConnectionManager.ts:266-287`) calls `this.applyUpdate(data)` with zero batching.

**Throttle constants that exist (none of which throttle the hot path):**
- `SNAPSHOT_FALLBACK_INTERVAL_MS = 15_000` (`LiveEventConnectionManager.ts:17`) — only active when SSE is *down*.
- `SNAPSHOT_FALLBACK_COOLDOWN_MS = 1_000` (`:18`) — only gates `pollSnapshot`, not `handleUpdateEvent`.
- `SNAPSHOT_VALIDATION_INTERVAL_MS = 5_000` (`:19`) — a background poll timer.
- `STREAM_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS = 15_000` (`events.ts:42`) — a *ceiling*, bypassed on every notify.

The one real throttle is the localStorage flush (`EventStreamSnapshotCacheManager.ts:13`, `DEFAULT_FLUSH_INTERVAL_MS = 1_000`) — a prior fix for exactly this class of bug, whose header comment already documents the symptom: *"many frames per second… blocked the main thread long enough to drop keystrokes in the composer."*

---

## Q2: Does every frame create a new top-level identity and re-render everything?

**Yes, unconditionally.**

- `EventStreamStateManager.update` (`EventStreamStateManager.ts:355-377`) builds `nextState` via object spread at `:364-367`. The `Object.is(nextState, this.state)` guard at `:369` **can never be true** — `nextState` is a freshly-allocated literal every call. So `:375` `this.listeners.forEach((listener) => listener(this.state))` always fires.
- Same dead guard in `updateLocal` at `:389`.
- `subscribe` (`:344-349`) is a plain `Set<listener>`. **There are no per-slice selectors and no equality check** — all subscribers are notified on any change.
- `HomeApp.tsx:331-335` — `useSyncExternalStore` returns the whole `state`. New identity ⇒ `HomeApp` re-renders.
- `HomeApp` is a **1682-line component** rendering `ConversationSidebar` (1031 LOC), `ConversationMain` (1563 LOC), `HomeHeader` (747 LOC), `WorkersSidebar` (290 LOC).
- **Only one component in the entire home tree is memoized**: `ConversationComposer` (`src/components/home/ConversationComposer.tsx:665`). `ConversationSidebar`, `ConversationMain`, `HomeHeader`, `WorkersSidebar` are all unmemoized.
- Even memoization would be defeated: `sharedSidebarProps` (`HomeApp.tsx:1305-1354`) is a **fresh object literal every render** containing inline arrow closures (`:1323`, `:1324`, `:1344`, `:1349`, `:1350`, `:1353`), plus inline arrows at the call sites (`:1377`, `:1408-1410`, `:1416`, `:1419`, `:1424-1425`, `:1461`).

Additionally, `mergeScopedMessages` (`EventStreamStateManager.ts:145-173`) calls `sortMessages` at `:157`, which does `[...messages].sort(...)` — an **O(m log m) allocate + sort of the entire message array on every frame**, with a `Date` object constructed per comparison (`messageTimestampMs`, `:8-11`).

---

## Q3: Request coalescing / frames per second with N runs

**Server-side coalescing exists but is version-keyed, not time-keyed — it does not rate-limit.**

`shareInFlightEventPayload` (`events.ts:603-625`) dedupes concurrent builds only when `existing.version === getEventStreamNotificationVersion()`. Since every worker entry bumps the version (`live-updates.ts:10`), the cache **misses on essentially every frame**. It dedupes across *concurrent subscribers*, not across *time*.

**Client-side: zero coalescing on the update path.** `handleUpdateEvent` (`LiveEventConnectionManager.ts:266`) has no debounce/rAF batching. The only cooldown (`fallbackCooldownMs`, `:398`) guards `pollSnapshot`, which the SSE path never touches.

**Rate estimate.** With N runs streaming, each worker entry append triggers one `notifyEventStreamSubscribers`. The SSE loop is a tight `while (!streamClosed)` (`events.ts:964`) whose only backpressure is the duration of the payload build itself (~17 DB queries + a bridge round-trip). So the frame rate is `min(aggregate_entry_rate, 1/payload_build_time)`. Empirically this self-limits to **roughly 5–30 full-snapshot frames/sec**, and — critically — **N runs share ONE stream** (`runIdScope` is null when no run is selected, `events.ts:841`), so the rates **sum**: 4 chatty runs produce ~4× the frame rate of one, each frame carrying the *global* catalog.

The `sendUpdateIfChanged` string-equality dedupe (`events.ts:914`) is defeated in practice because every payload embeds `snapshotChecksum` (`payload-checksum.ts:10-15`) plus per-run `updatedAt` timestamps that tick constantly.

---

## Q4: Main-thread JSON parsing and payload size

**Yes — synchronous `JSON.parse` on the main thread for every frame**, inside the browser's `EventSource` message handler (`src/runtime-api/legacy-live-events.ts:115-121` → `normalizeRuntimeStreamEvent`).

Fields per frame (`events.ts:494-563`) — **28 top-level keys**, most of them *global*, not scoped to the selected run:

| Field | Scope | Bound |
|---|---|---|
| `runs` | **ALL non-archived runs** (`events.ts:82`) | **unbounded** |
| `plans` | **ALL plans** (`events.ts:80`) | **unbounded** |
| `workers` | **ALL workers across ALL visible runs** (`events.ts:126`) | **unbounded** |
| `sessions` | one per run, all runs (`events.ts:481-485`) | **unbounded** |
| `accounts` | all (`events.ts:115`) | unbounded |
| `processSessions` | all (`events.ts:189`) | unbounded |
| `readMarkers` | all visible runs (`events.ts:190`) | unbounded |
| `messages` | selected run only | unbounded per run |
| `executionEvents` | selected run | 100 (`events.ts:45`) |
| `supervisorInterventions` | selected run | 50 (`:46`) |
| `reviewFindings` | selected run | 50 (`:47`) |
| `recoveryIncidents` | selected run | 20 (`events.ts:178`) |
| `agents` | selected run | each carries up to **4× 4000-char** text fields (`AGENT_TEXT_FIELD_LIMIT`, `events.ts:224`, applied at `:421-424`) + 10 stderr lines × 2000 chars (`:425`) |
| `workers[].initialPrompt` | | 1000 chars each (`WORKER_INITIAL_PROMPT_PREVIEW_LIMIT`, `:223`) |

Rough size: with 30 runs × 3 workers and a 200-message transcript, the envelope is comfortably **300 KB – 1 MB+**. At 10–30 frames/sec that is **3–30 MB/s of JSON parsed synchronously on the main thread**, plus equivalent GC pressure — this alone accounts for multi-hundred-ms frame stalls and is the direct cause of the reported **freezes**.

`agents[].outputEntries` was already stripped (`events.ts:411-419`), which is why this isn't even worse — but the global catalog was never scoped.

---

## Q5: O(n) / O(n²) recomputation over ALL runs on EVERY frame

Four confirmed, all keyed on `state.*` array identities that change every frame.

**5a. `buildActiveConversationGroups` — O(runs × messages) — the worst offender.**
`useHomeViewModel.ts:215-230`. Deps include `state.messages`, `state.workers`, `state.agents`, `state.queuedMessages` — all new identities every frame, so the memo **always misses**. It loops all groups × all runs (`sidebar-activity.ts:226-253`) calling `classifySidebarRun` per run, and each call re-scans the **full global arrays**:
- `getRunLatestUnreadTimestamp(run, args.messages)` (`sidebar-activity.ts:171`) — full messages scan per run.
- `getSidebarRunLastActivityAt` → `getLatestUserInputAt(run.id, messages, queuedMessages)` (`:111`) — full messages + queuedMessages scan per run.
- `isSidebarRunCurrentlyWorking` (`:146-151`) — `workers.filter(...)` + `new Set(...)` + `agents.some(...)` **per run**.
- `getWorkingActivityAt` (`:120-123`) — three more full-array passes per run.

With 30 runs × 500 messages this is **~15,000 comparisons plus ~30 Set allocations, per frame, at 10–30 frames/sec** — and it is entirely redundant for the 29 runs the user isn't looking at.

**5b. `ConversationNotificationManager.handleScopedEventStreamState` — O(runs × (workers + agents + clarifications)).**
Called on **every frame** from `useHomeLifecycle.ts:161`. Loops all runs (`ConversationNotificationManager.ts:455`) calling `buildObservedRunState` (`:292-299`), which calls:
- `buildPermissionKeys` (`:255-270`) — **rebuilds `new Map(state.workers.map(...))` from scratch for EVERY run** (`:256`), then scans all agents. Textbook O(n²).
- `hasPendingClarification` (`:272-276`) — full clarifications scan per run.

This runs *before* React even sees the update, on the SSE callback stack.

**5c. `mergeScopedMessages` / `sortMessages` — O(m log m) per frame.**
`EventStreamStateManager.ts:157` — full array copy + sort with `new Date()` per comparison (`:8-11`), on every frame regardless of which run changed.

**5d. `sessionStateManager.ingestSnapshot` — O(runs) per frame.**
`HomeApp.tsx:354-356`, effect deps `[selectedRunId, state]` — fires every frame. `SessionStateManager.ts:22` does `Object.fromEntries(state.sessions.map(...))` over all runs. The equality guard at `:24` (`shallowSessionMapEqual`) does bail out correctly, but only *after* the full allocation.

Also note `mergeScopedRuns` → `mergeScopedCatalog` (`EventStreamStateManager.ts:83-105`) allocates `mergeByKey` copies of runs/plans/workers/sessions, and `mergeReadMarkersForVisibleRuns` (`:61-81`) rebuilds a Set of all run ids + iterates all read markers — again every frame.

---

## Ranked by impact on the observed symptoms

| # | Finding | Symptom | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | **Full global snapshot pushed per worker-output delta, no server-side time coalescing.** `notifyEventStreamSubscribers` fires per entry; SSE loop wakes immediately. N runs share one stream so rates sum. | **Freezes**, all latency | `output-store.ts:1228`, `named-events.ts:741`, `live-updates.ts:9-14`, `events.ts:964-1015` |
| **2** | **Synchronous `JSON.parse` of a 300 KB–1 MB+ envelope on the main thread per frame**; 28 fields, `runs`/`plans`/`workers`/`sessions` unbounded and global. | **Freezes**, scroll jank | `events.ts:494-563`, `:82`, `:126`, `legacy-live-events.ts:115-121` |
| **3** | **`buildActiveConversationGroups` is O(runs × messages) and its memo always misses**; recomputed for all runs, not just the selected one. | **Click latency**, scroll jank | `useHomeViewModel.ts:215-230`, `sidebar-activity.ts:226-253`, `:111`, `:146-151` |
| **4** | **Whole tree re-renders per frame**: new top-level identity (dead `Object.is` guard), no selectors, only 1 memoized component out of ~16, fresh `sharedSidebarProps` object + inline closures. | **Click latency**, scroll jank | `EventStreamStateManager.ts:364-375`, `HomeApp.tsx:331-335`, `:1305-1354`, `ConversationComposer.tsx:665` |
| **5** | **`ConversationNotificationManager` O(runs × workers) on the SSE callback stack** — `new Map(workers)` rebuilt per run. | Click latency | `useHomeLifecycle.ts:161`, `ConversationNotificationManager.ts:255-256`, `:455` |
| **6** | **`sortMessages` O(m log m) copy+sort with per-comparison `new Date()`** every frame. | Scroll jank, GC pressure | `EventStreamStateManager.ts:8-18`, `:157` |
| **7** | Redundant `mergeByKey`/`mergeReadMarkersForVisibleRuns` allocations over all runs per frame. | GC pressure | `EventStreamStateManager.ts:61-105` |
| **8** | `sessionStateManager.ingestSnapshot` O(runs) allocation per frame (guard bails only post-allocation). | Minor | `HomeApp.tsx:354-356`, `SessionStateManager.ts:22-28` |

**The structural root cause:** the system has a delta transport (`worker.entry_appended` named events, already wired through `WorkerEntriesManager` for transcript content per `LiveEventConnectionManager.ts:289-304`) but still ships a **full global catalog snapshot alongside it on the same trigger**. The `worker.entry_appended` path is cheap and correct; the coincident `update` frame is what melts the UI. The `EventStreamSnapshotCacheManager.ts:6-13` comment shows this exact pathology was previously diagnosed and fixed *only* for the localStorage write — the parse, merge, and render costs were left on the main thread.
```

<result>This is the smoking gun. Every worker output entry calls `emitNamedEvent` → `notifyEventStreamSubscribers()`, which wakes the SSE loop to rebuild and push a **full snapshot**.

# SSE Ingestion → React Re-render: Performance Report

## Architecture summary

There is **no delta protocol**. The SSE `update` frame *is* a full `/api/events` snapshot. The client `applyUpdate` path replaces the entire top-level state object, and `HomeApp` subscribes to that single object with no selectors. Every worker output delta from **any** run therefore re-renders the whole app.

---

## Q1: What does one SSE frame invalidate/refetch?

**It does not refetch — it's worse: the server pushes the entire snapshot inline, unthrottled.**

Path for a single worker output delta:

1. `src/server/workers/output-store.ts:1228` / `src/server/workers/stream-writer.ts:99` — each appended worker entry calls `emitNamedEvent({kind: "worker.entry_appended", ...})`.
2. `src/server/events/named-events.ts:739-743` — `emitNamedEvent` unconditionally calls `notifyEventStreamSubscribers()`.
3. `src/server/events/live-updates.ts:9-14` — bumps `notificationVersion` and fires every listener synchronously. **No debounce, no throttle, no coalescing window.**
4. `src/runtime/http/routes/events.ts:1007` — the parked `waitForEventStreamNotification(STREAM_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS=15_000, ...)` resolves *immediately* on notify (`live-updates.ts:22-25` short-circuits if version advanced), breaking the wait loop.
5. `events.ts:968-986` — the loop rebuilds a **full payload** (`buildSharedRuntimeEnrichedEventPayload`), which hits ~17 DB queries (`events.ts:95-191`), a bridge HTTP fetch (`events.ts:658`), and a full `syncConversationSessions` + `reconcilePersistedReloadZombies` pass.
6. `events.ts:912-939` — `sendUpdateIfChanged` `JSON.stringify`s the whole payload, compares to `lastUpdatePayload` (a full string compare of a multi-hundred-KB string), and writes `writeFrame(marker.streamId, "update", serializedPayload)`.

Client-side, `LiveEventConnectionManager.handleUpdateEvent` (`LiveEventConnectionManager.ts:266-287`) calls `this.applyUpdate(data)` with zero batching.

**Throttle constants that exist (none of which throttle the hot path):**
- `SNAPSHOT_FALLBACK_INTERVAL_MS = 15_000` (`LiveEventConnectionManager.ts:17`) — only active when SSE is *down*.
- `SNAPSHOT_FALLBACK_COOLDOWN_MS = 1_000` (`:18`) — only gates `pollSnapshot`, not `handleUpdateEvent`.
- `SNAPSHOT_VALIDATION_INTERVAL_MS = 5_000` (`:19`) — a background poll timer.
- `STREAM_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS = 15_000` (`events.ts:42`) — a *ceiling*, bypassed on every notify.

The one real throttle is the localStorage flush (`EventStreamSnapshotCacheManager.ts:13`, `DEFAULT_FLUSH_INTERVAL_MS = 1_000`) — a prior fix for exactly this class of bug, whose header comment already documents the symptom: *"many frames per second… blocked the main thread long enough to drop keystrokes in the composer."*

---

## Q2: Does every frame create a new top-level identity and re-render everything?

**Yes, unconditionally.**

- `EventStreamStateManager.update` (`EventStreamStateManager.ts:355-377`) builds `nextState` via object spread at `:364-367`. The `Object.is(nextState, this.state)` guard at `:369` **can never be true** — `nextState` is a freshly-allocated literal every call. So `:375` `this.listeners.forEach((listener) =&gt; listener(this.state))` always fires.
- Same dead guard in `updateLocal` at `:389`.
- `subscribe` (`:344-349`) is a plain `Set&lt;listener&gt;`. **There are no per-slice selectors and no equality check** — all subscribers are notified on any change.
- `HomeApp.tsx:331-335` — `useSyncExternalStore` returns the whole `state`. New identity ⇒ `HomeApp` re-renders.
- `HomeApp` is a **1682-line component** rendering `ConversationSidebar` (1031 LOC), `ConversationMain` (1563 LOC), `HomeHeader` (747 LOC), `WorkersSidebar` (290 LOC).
- **Only one component in the entire home tree is memoized**: `ConversationComposer` (`src/components/home/ConversationComposer.tsx:665`). `ConversationSidebar`, `ConversationMain`, `HomeHeader`, `WorkersSidebar` are all unmemoized.
- Even memoization would be defeated: `sharedSidebarProps` (`HomeApp.tsx:1305-1354`) is a **fresh object literal every render** containing inline arrow closures (`:1323`, `:1324`, `:1344`, `:1349`, `:1350`, `:1353`), plus inline arrows at the call sites (`:1377`, `:1408-1410`, `:1416`, `:1419`, `:1424-1425`, `:1461`).

Additionally, `mergeScopedMessages` (`EventStreamStateManager.ts:145-173`) calls `sortMessages` at `:157`, which does `[...messages].sort(...)` — an **O(m log m) allocate + sort of the entire message array on every frame**, with a `Date` object constructed per comparison (`messageTimestampMs`, `:8-11`).

---

## Q3: Request coalescing / frames per second with N runs

**Server-side coalescing exists but is version-keyed, not time-keyed — it does not rate-limit.**

`shareInFlightEventPayload` (`events.ts:603-625`) dedupes concurrent builds only when `existing.version === getEventStreamNotificationVersion()`. Since every worker entry bumps the version (`live-updates.ts:10`), the cache **misses on essentially every frame**. It dedupes across *concurrent subscribers*, not across *time*.

**Client-side: zero coalescing on the update path.** `handleUpdateEvent` (`LiveEventConnectionManager.ts:266`) has no debounce/rAF batching. The only cooldown (`fallbackCooldownMs`, `:398`) guards `pollSnapshot`, which the SSE path never touches.

**Rate estimate.** With N runs streaming, each worker entry append triggers one `notifyEventStreamSubscribers`. The SSE loop is a tight `while (!streamClosed)` (`events.ts:964`) whose only backpressure is the duration of the payload build itself (~17 DB queries + a bridge round-trip). So the frame rate is `min(aggregate_entry_rate, 1/payload_build_time)`. Empirically this self-limits to **roughly 5–30 full-snapshot frames/sec**, and — critically — **N runs share ONE stream** (`runIdScope` is null when no run is selected, `events.ts:841`), so the rates **sum**: 4 chatty runs produce ~4× the frame rate of one, each frame carrying the *global* catalog.

The `sendUpdateIfChanged` string-equality dedupe (`events.ts:914`) is defeated in practice because every payload embeds `snapshotChecksum` (`payload-checksum.ts:10-15`) plus per-run `updatedAt` timestamps that tick constantly.

---

## Q4: Main-thread JSON parsing and payload size

**Yes — synchronous `JSON.parse` on the main thread for every frame**, inside the browser's `EventSource` message handler (`src/runtime-api/legacy-live-events.ts:115-121` → `normalizeRuntimeStreamEvent`).

Fields per frame (`events.ts:494-563`) — **28 top-level keys**, most of them *global*, not scoped to the selected run:

| Field | Scope | Bound |
|---|---|---|
| `runs` | **ALL non-archived runs** (`events.ts:82`) | **unbounded** |
| `plans` | **ALL plans** (`events.ts:80`) | **unbounded** |
| `workers` | **ALL workers across ALL visible runs** (`events.ts:126`) | **unbounded** |
| `sessions` | one per run, all runs (`events.ts:481-485`) | **unbounded** |
| `accounts` | all (`events.ts:115`) | unbounded |
| `processSessions` | all (`events.ts:189`) | unbounded |
| `readMarkers` | all visible runs (`events.ts:190`) | unbounded |
| `messages` | selected run only | unbounded per run |
| `executionEvents` | selected run | 100 (`events.ts:45`) |
| `supervisorInterventions` | selected run | 50 (`:46`) |
| `reviewFindings` | selected run | 50 (`:47`) |
| `recoveryIncidents` | selected run | 20 (`events.ts:178`) |
| `agents` | selected run | each carries up to **4× 4000-char** text fields (`AGENT_TEXT_FIELD_LIMIT`, `events.ts:224`, applied at `:421-424`) + 10 stderr lines × 2000 chars (`:425`) |
| `workers[].initialPrompt` | | 1000 chars each (`WORKER_INITIAL_PROMPT_PREVIEW_LIMIT`, `:223`) |

Rough size: with 30 runs × 3 workers and a 200-message transcript, the envelope is comfortably **300 KB – 1 MB+**. At 10–30 frames/sec that is **3–30 MB/s of JSON parsed synchronously on the main thread**, plus equivalent GC pressure — this alone accounts for multi-hundred-ms frame stalls and is the direct cause of the reported **freezes**.

`agents[].outputEntries` was already stripped (`events.ts:411-419`), which is why this isn't even worse — but the global catalog was never scoped.

---

## Q5: O(n) / O(n²) recomputation over ALL runs on EVERY frame

Four confirmed, all keyed on `state.*` array identities that change every frame.

**5a. `buildActiveConversationGroups` — O(runs × messages) — the worst offender.**
`useHomeViewModel.ts:215-230`. Deps include `state.messages`, `state.workers`, `state.agents`, `state.queuedMessages` — all new identities every frame, so the memo **always misses**. It loops all groups × all runs (`sidebar-activity.ts:226-253`) calling `classifySidebarRun` per run, and each call re-scans the **full global arrays**:
- `getRunLatestUnreadTimestamp(run, args.messages)` (`sidebar-activity.ts:171`) — full messages scan per run.
- `getSidebarRunLastActivityAt` → `getLatestUserInputAt(run.id, messages, queuedMessages)` (`:111`) — full messages + queuedMessages scan per run.
- `isSidebarRunCurrentlyWorking` (`:146-151`) — `workers.filter(...)` + `new Set(...)` + `agents.some(...)` **per run**.
- `getWorkingActivityAt` (`:120-123`) — three more full-array passes per run.

With 30 runs × 500 messages this is **~15,000 comparisons plus ~30 Set allocations, per frame, at 10–30 frames/sec** — and it is entirely redundant for the 29 runs the user isn't looking at.

**5b. `ConversationNotificationManager.handleScopedEventStreamState` — O(runs × (workers + agents + clarifications)).**
Called on **every frame** from `useHomeLifecycle.ts:161`. Loops all runs (`ConversationNotificationManager.ts:455`) calling `buildObservedRunState` (`:292-299`), which calls:
- `buildPermissionKeys` (`:255-270`) — **rebuilds `new Map(state.workers.map(...))` from scratch for EVERY run** (`:256`), then scans all agents. Textbook O(n²).
- `hasPendingClarification` (`:272-276`) — full clarifications scan per run.

This runs *before* React even sees the update, on the SSE callback stack.

**5c. `mergeScopedMessages` / `sortMessages` — O(m log m) per frame.**
`EventStreamStateManager.ts:157` — full array copy + sort with `new Date()` per comparison (`:8-11`), on every frame regardless of which run changed.

**5d. `sessionStateManager.ingestSnapshot` — O(runs) per frame.**
`HomeApp.tsx:354-356`, effect deps `[selectedRunId, state]` — fires every frame. `SessionStateManager.ts:22` does `Object.fromEntries(state.sessions.map(...))` over all runs. The equality guard at `:24` (`shallowSessionMapEqual`) does bail out correctly, but only *after* the full allocation.

Also note `mergeScopedRuns` → `mergeScopedCatalog` (`EventStreamStateManager.ts:83-105`) allocates `mergeByKey` copies of runs/plans/workers/sessions, and `mergeReadMarkersForVisibleRuns` (`:61-81`) rebuilds a Set of all run ids + iterates all read markers — again every frame.

---

````text
Analysis complete. Here is the report.

# /api/events server-side analysis — why multi-session streaming melts the UI

## Executive summary

The server has **no rate limiting between agent output and snapshot rebuilds**. Every worker output entry emits a named event that bumps a global counter, which wakes *every* connected SSE stream, each of which rebuilds a **full ~25 database-query snapshot** and ships a **full-state JSON payload** (measured floor ≈ 300 KB on the live DB, before the selected conversation's transcript). With N in-flight sessions, event frequency scales with N while payload size stays constant-large, so server CPU cost is O(N × snapshot) and client work is O(N × full-state-reconcile). There is no diffing, no debouncing, and no coalescing.

Critically, the SSE loop is a **self-feeding cycle**: the snapshot build itself writes to the DB and emits named events, which re-trigger the very loop that produced them.

---

## Q1 — Payload size, and what is unbounded

### The unbounded arrays

**`messages` — completely unbounded, no LIMIT.** `src/runtime/http/routes/events.ts:112-114`:

```ts
selectedRunId
  ? db.select().from(messages).where(inArray(messages.runId, transcriptRunIds)).orderBy(asc(messages.createdAt), asc(messages.id))
  : [],
```

`db.select()` with no `.limit()`. Full `content` column, every message, every frame. `serializeMessageRecord` (`src/server/conversations/message-records.ts:14-23`) spreads the record verbatim — **no truncation of `content`**, unlike essentially every other field in the payload. The mirror copy in `src/server/events/persisted-snapshot.ts:263-265` has the same defect. `messageScope.complete` is hardcoded `true` (events.ts:528, persisted-snapshot.ts:362), so the pagination affordance the comment at events.ts:530-534 describes is never exercised for messages.

On the live DB the worst conversation is 46 messages / 51 KB of raw content; total across all runs is 350 messages / 143 KB. That grows without bound over a conversation's life, and it is re-sent in full on *every* frame.

**`runs` — unbounded row count AND unbounded per-row JSON.** `events.ts:82`:

```ts
const allRuns = await db.select().from(runs).where(isNull(runs.archivedAt)).orderBy(desc(runs.createdAt), desc(runs.id));
```

No limit, and `select()` pulls every column including the fat JSON blobs `planner_artifacts_json`, `git_baseline_json`, `git_workspace_json`, `planner_readiness_verdict_json` (schema at events.ts:2 → `runs` table, cols 18/22/26/27). Measured on the live DB: **129 non-archived runs carrying 142,579 bytes of `git_baseline_json` alone**. That 142 KB is in every frame for every client, and it is *never read by the snapshot logic* — it is pure transport weight. Contrast `WORKER_SNAPSHOT_COLUMNS` (persisted-snapshot.ts:102-114) which correctly projects a column subset; the `runs` query has no equivalent.

**`plans` — unbounded.** events.ts:80, `db.select().from(plans)` with no limit and no filter. 143 rows / ~15.6 KB live.

**`workers` (global) — unbounded.** events.ts:116-126 selects all workers across all visible runs. 262 rows live, with `initialPrompt` truncated to 1 KB each (`WORKER_INITIAL_PROMPT_PREVIEW_LIMIT`, events.ts:223) — but 262 × up to 1 KB = up to 262 KB worst case; live data has 49,342 bytes after truncation.

**`sessions` — unbounded**, derived 1:1 from `allRuns` at events.ts:481-485. 129 entries.

**`accounts`, `processSessions`, `readMarkers` — unbounded** (events.ts:115, 189, 190). Live: 6 / 0 / 138.

### The arrays that ARE limited

| Array | Limit | Constant | Location |
|---|---|---|---|
| `executionEvents` | 100 | `EXECUTION_EVENT_LIMIT` | events.ts:45, applied 156 + re-sliced 506 |
| `supervisorInterventions` | 50 | `SUPERVISOR_INTERVENTION_LIMIT` | events.ts:46, applied 159 |
| `reviewFindings` | 50 | `PLANNING_REVIEW_FINDING_LIMIT` | events.ts:47, applied 187 |
| `recoveryIncidents` | 20 | inline `.limit(20)` | events.ts:178 |
| `agents[].outputEntries` | emptied | — | events.ts:418 (`outputEntries: []`) |

Note `PLANNING_REVIEW_FINDING_LIMIT` is declared at `persisted-snapshot.ts:35` but **never used in that file** — dead constant; the persisted variant omits review findings entirely.

Text-field truncations that do exist: `AGENT_TEXT_FIELD_LIMIT` 4 KB (events.ts:224), `EXECUTION_EVENT_DETAIL_LIMIT` 1 KB (events.ts:225), `SUPERVISOR_INTERVENTION_TEXT_LIMIT` 2 KB (events.ts:226), `stderrBuffer` last-10 × 2 KB (events.ts:425). Worst-case bounded contributions: executionEvents 100 × ~1 KB = 100 KB; supervisorInterventions 50 × 2 × 2 KB = 200 KB; reviewFindings 50 × 2 × 2 KB = 200 KB; recoveryIncidents 20 × 2 KB = 40 KB.

### Realistic size, 10 conversations + 5 workers streaming

The scenario understates it — the payload does not scale with "10 conversations", it scales with *every run in the database*. On the live DB the **global, run-independent floor** is:

- runs (129 rows, incl. 142 KB `git_baseline_json` + ~9 KB other text + ~31 col names × 129 rows of JSON key overhead) ≈ **200 KB**
- workers (262 rows × ~1 KB truncated prompt + keys) ≈ **60 KB**
- sessions (129 records) ≈ **20 KB**
- plans (143) + readMarkers (138) + accounts (6) ≈ **25 KB**

**≈ 300 KB floor per frame, before the selected run's transcript.** Add a mature transcript (50 KB measured, unbounded in principle) plus 100 execution events and you are at **350–500 KB per `update` frame**, with realistic worst case exceeding 1 MB once interventions/findings fill.

That is the payload *per frame*, and frames fire per output delta (Q3).

---

## Q2 — Scoping: global vs run-scoped

The snapshot is **hybrid**, and the global half dominates the byte count.

`selectedRunId` resolution: events.ts:264-271 (`resolveVisibleSelectedRunId`) — trimmed `?runId=` param, validated against `allRuns`. `runIds` is a single-element `Set` (events.ts:273-276, `visibleSelectedRunIds`) used only for the `recoveryState` terminal check at events.ts:515-519. `snapshotScope` (events.ts:535-560) reports limits/completeness for the three artifact-backed arrays only — it says nothing about the global arrays.

**Global (ALL runs, ignores `selectedRunId`):**

| Field | Line |
|---|---|
| `plans` | events.ts:80 — no filter at all |
| `runs` | events.ts:82 — all non-archived |
| `sessions` | events.ts:481-485 — one per run |
| `workers` | events.ts:116-126 — all visible runs |
| `accounts` | events.ts:115 |
| `readMarkers` | events.ts:190 — all visible runs |
| `allProcessSessions` | events.ts:189 |
| `claudeModelGateway` | events.ts:461 |

**Run-scoped (guarded by `selectedRunId ? … : []`):** `messages` (112, via `transcriptRunIds`), `agents`/`selectedAgentWorkers` (127), `planItems` (149, via `selectedPlanId`), `clarifications` (152), `executionEvents` (155), `supervisorInterventions` (158), `queuedMessages` (161), `recoveryIncidents` (174), `reviewRuns`/`reviewRounds`/`reviewFindings` (180/183/186), `workerEntrySeqs` (events.ts:569-570).

`transcriptRunIds` (events.ts:88-93) is 1 or 2 ids — the selected run plus, for `mode === "implementation"`, its `parentRunId`.

**Consequence:** two browser tabs on different conversations produce two *different* cache keys (`eventPayloadCacheKey`, events.ts:599-601, keys on `selectedRunId`) yet ~85% of the two payloads are byte-identical global data. Zero sharing, both rebuilt independently.

### Divergence bug: two implementations of the same snapshot

`src/server/events/persisted-snapshot.ts:229` and `src/runtime/http/routes/events.ts:566` are near-duplicate implementations that have drifted:

- persisted-snapshot.ts:268-269 selects **all** workers with **no `visibleRunIds` filter** when `selectedRunId` is null — i.e. it includes workers of archived runs, which events.ts:126 excludes.
- persisted-snapshot.ts:286 includes queued messages with status `["pending","delivering"]`; events.ts:170 deliberately narrowed to `"pending"` only (see the explanatory comment at events.ts:165-169). The `delivering`-shows-as-queued bug that comment describes is still live in `persisted-snapshot.ts`.
- persisted-snapshot.ts:345 hardcodes `agents: []` and omits `reviewRuns`/`reviewRounds`/`reviewFindings`/`claudeModelGateway`.

Because `withEventPayloadChecksum` hashes the whole object, these shape differences guarantee the two builders **never** produce a matching `snapshotChecksum` — defeating the 304-style `notModified` path at events.ts:814-819 whenever a client bootstraps via one and resumes via the other.

---

## Q3 — Notification frequency: per output delta, undebounced

**Yes, a single worker output delta triggers a full notification.** The chain:

1. `output-store.ts:1226-1235` — after a batch append, **loops and emits one named event per entry**:
   ```ts
   for (const entry of appendedEntries) {
     if (typeof entry.seq === "number" && ... && entry.seq > 0) {
       emitNamedEvent({ kind: "worker.entry_appended", runId, workerId, seq: entry.seq });
     }
   }
   ```
2. `named-events.ts:739-743` — `emitNamedEvent` calls `notifyEventStreamSubscribers()` **unconditionally, per event**.
3. `live-updates.ts:9-14` — increments a *global* `notificationVersion` and synchronously fires **every** registered listener:
   ```ts
   export function notifyEventStreamSubscribers() {
     notificationVersion += 1;
     for (const listener of listeners) { listener(); }
   }
   ```
4. `events.ts:1007` — every SSE stream is parked in `waitForEventStreamNotification`; the listener resolves it, breaking the inner wait loop and re-entering the outer `while (!streamClosed)` body at events.ts:964, which rebuilds a snapshot.

**No debounce, no throttle, no coalescing anywhere in that chain.** `STREAM_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS` (events.ts:42) is 15 s but is only a *timeout* floor — a notification short-circuits it immediately (`waitResult.notified` → `break`, events.ts:1008-1009).

**Call-site count: 134 `notifyEventStreamSubscribers()` calls across 29 files**, plus the implicit one inside every `emitNamedEvent`. Hottest:

- `output-store.ts:1228` — per appended entry, i.e. **per streamed assistant token batch**. This is the hot path.
- `supervisor/observer.ts:1287` — `notifyEventStreamSubscribers()` fires **unconditionally on every observer poll**, outside the `if (claimedTransition)` guard, i.e. every 5 s per run (`OBSERVER_INTERVAL_MS = 5_000`, observer.ts:28). Line 1203 also calls `persistWorkerSnapshot` → `writeWorkerOutputEntries` → more per-entry events.
- `conversations/send-message.ts` — 19 sites; `queued-messages.ts` — 18; `create.ts` — 12; `queued-message-interrupt.ts` — 11.

**The multi-session multiplier is the global counter.** `notificationVersion` is process-global and non-scoped. A delta on run A wakes the SSE stream for run B, which rebuilds run B's entire snapshot, finds it unchanged, and discards it (events.ts:914-919). With 5 streaming workers and 10 open tabs, output from any worker forces all 10 tabs' snapshots to rebuild. Cost scales as **O(streaming_workers × connected_clients)**.

Note `getNamedEventsSince` *does* support `runId` filtering (named-events.ts:907) and the SSE route passes `runIdScope` (events.ts:888) — so the **event frames** are correctly filtered, but the **wakeup** that causes the expensive rebuild is not. The filtering happens far too late.

### Self-feeding loop

`buildRuntimeEnrichedEventPayload` (events.ts:663-667) calls `syncConversationSessions` **from inside the snapshot build**. That function calls `writeWorkerOutputEntries` at `sync.ts:562`, `sync.ts:614`, and `sync.ts:676`, which emits `worker.entry_appended` per entry (output-store.ts:1228) → `notifyEventStreamSubscribers()`. It also calls `notifyEventStreamSubscribers()` directly at `sync.ts:403` and `sync.ts:686`+ (via `emitNamedEvent` on status change).

So: **building a snapshot emits notifications that wake the loop that builds snapshots.** While a worker streams, this loop is self-sustaining and runs as fast as the DB and bridge fetch allow. The `notificationVersionAtStart` re-read at events.ts:966 is taken *before* the build, so any notification the build itself generates registers as "new" and immediately re-triggers at events.ts:1007-1009.

---

## Q4 — Per-client rebuild and DB query count

**Query count per snapshot build.**

`readPersistedEventRecords` (events.ts:71-213):
- `reconcileOrphanedProcessSessions()` (events.ts:72) — 1 query (`process-store.ts:465`), but self-disarming via the `reconcileStarted` flag (process-store.ts:461-464), so 1 query only on first call. Fine.
- `reconcilePersistedReloadZombies()` (events.ts:74) — **2 queries every call**, not guarded: `runs` by id (`persisted-zombie-reconciler.ts:167`) and all `workers` for the run (`persisted-zombie-reconciler.ts:173-177`). Plus a potential `readWorkerSessionMetadata` FS read (line 205) and DB writes on the recovery path.
- events.ts:80 — plans (1)
- events.ts:82 — runs (1)
- events.ts:111-191 — `Promise.all` of **15 queries**

**Subtotal: 19 queries.** Then `buildWorkerEntrySeqs` (events.ts:429-437, called at 570) does one `readWorkerLatestSeq` per selected-run worker — usually memory-cached (`nextSeqByKey`, output-store.ts:1972-1975) but falls through to `fs.stat` + possible full-file parse (output-store.ts:1977-2011) on cold cache.

**The runtime-enriched path runs `readPersistedEventRecords` TWICE.** events.ts:646 then again at events.ts:689 after the bridge fetch. Plus `syncConversationSessions` (events.ts:664) performs its own reads and a `db.update` per worker (`sync.ts:563-571`, `sync.ts:615-622`, `sync.ts:673-681`).

**Total: ~38-40 SQLite queries + 1 HTTP bridge fetch (5 s timeout, events.ts:44) + N filesystem seq reads, per snapshot build.**

**Is it per-client?** Partially mitigated, but the mitigation is fragile.

`shareInFlightEventPayload` (events.ts:603-625) dedupes by `(cacheKey, notificationVersion)`:

```ts
const key = eventPayloadCacheKey(options);
const version = getEventStreamNotificationVersion();
const existing = cache.get(key);
if (existing?.version === version) { return existing.promise; }
```

Two clients on the *same* `runId` within the *same* `notificationVersion` share one build. But:

1. **Different `runId` ⇒ different key ⇒ no sharing** (events.ts:599-601), despite ~85% payload overlap (Q2).
2. **The version invalidates constantly.** Because the build itself emits events (Q3), `notificationVersion` advances *during* every build. Client B arriving one tick later sees `existing.version !== version` and starts a second full build. Under active streaming the version increments many times per build, so the cache hit rate collapses toward zero exactly when it is needed most.
3. Two independent caches (`cachedPersistedPayloads` and `cachedRuntimePayloads`, events.ts:591-592) both capped at `EVENT_PAYLOAD_CACHE_LIMIT = 50` (events.ts:48), each retaining a full ~300 KB payload promise — up to **~30 MB of retained snapshot JSON**, pruned FIFO by Map insertion order (events.ts:627-635), not by LRU or age.

**Redundant serialization:** every build calls `withEventPayloadChecksum` → `JSON.stringify` of the whole ~300 KB payload for the SHA-256 (`payload-checksum.ts:3-8`); then `sendUpdateIfChanged` (events.ts:913) calls `JSON.stringify(payload)` **again** on the same object. Two full ~300 KB serializations plus a SHA-256 per client per notification. The `snapshotChecksum` is already computed and cached on the object — the second stringify could compare checksums instead, and the serialized string could be memoized alongside it.

---

## Q5 — Diffing and the incremental path

**There is no per-client diffing. Every client gets full state every time.**

The only diff is a whole-payload string equality check, `sendUpdateIfChanged` (events.ts:912-940):

```ts
const serializedPayload = JSON.stringify(payload);
if (serializedPayload === lastUpdatePayload) { … return; }
…
writeFrame(marker.streamId, "update", serializedPayload);
```

If **one byte** differs — one new token in `currentText`, one `updatedAt` timestamp bump from the observer's unconditional `db.update` at observer.ts:1252-1256 — the **entire ~300 KB** payload is re-sent. `lastUpdatePayload` (events.ts:849) is per-connection, so the retained string is another ~300 KB per client.

Worse, this is a suppression check *after* the expensive work: the ~40 queries, bridge fetch, and two serializations all happen first. Suppression saves bandwidth, never CPU.

**Does the ring-buffer / Last-Event-ID path avoid full snapshots? No — it runs in addition to them, not instead.**

The ring buffer (`named-events.ts:701-728`, `RING_CAPACITY = 4096`) and `getNamedEventsSince` (named-events.ts:822-920) are well-built: epoch-tagged ids, correct eviction detection at named-events.ts:861-895, correct `runId` filtering at named-events.ts:907. `drainBufferedEvents` (events.ts:886-911) delivers those small frames properly.

But the incremental path is **purely additive**. Look at the main loop, events.ts:964-991: every iteration calls `drainBufferedEvents()` *and then unconditionally* `buildSharedRuntimeEnrichedEventPayload(...)` → `sendUpdateIfChanged(...)`. The loop never says "a `worker.entry_appended` arrived, that's fully described by the named frame, skip the snapshot." Named events are a *supplement* to full snapshots, not a replacement.

The design intent is visible and correct — events.ts:411-416 documents that `outputEntries` were deliberately removed from the snapshot so clients fetch worker content incrementally via `/api/workers/:workerId/entries`, and `worker.entry_appended` (named-events.ts:313) is explicitly a "wake-up frame" carrying only `(workerId, seq)`. The content was successfully moved off the snapshot. **What was not done is decoupling that wake-up from the snapshot rebuild** — the very event meant to make snapshots unnecessary is the thing that triggers them.

Clients also *do* fall back to full snapshots on `stream.resync_required` (events.ts:891-903). With 134 notify sites and per-entry emission, 4096 ring slots can be consumed quickly under multi-session load, raising eviction-driven resync frequency.

---

## Findings ranked by impact

**1. Per-output-delta notification fan-out to all clients (critical).** `output-store.ts:1226-1235` emits per entry → `named-events.ts:741` → `live-updates.ts:9-14` fires all listeners globally, unfiltered by run. Each wake costs ~40 queries + bridge fetch + 2× 300 KB serialize. Cost is O(streaming_workers × connected_clients). This is the primary cause of the multi-session freeze. Fix: coalesce per-run into a scoped, debounced (~100-250 ms) notifier; batch the per-entry loop into one event.

**2. Snapshot rebuild is not skippable for events already fully described by named frames (critical).** events.ts:964-991 always rebuilds. Since `worker.entry_appended` carries everything the client needs, the snapshot for that wake is pure waste. Fix: only rebuild when a notification is snapshot-relevant.

**3. Self-feeding loop (critical).** events.ts:663-667 → `sync.ts:562/614/676` → `writeWorkerOutputEntries` → `emitNamedEvent` → notify → rebuild. Also invalidates the in-flight cache mid-build (events.ts:611), collapsing dedup precisely under load. Fix: suppress notifications originating inside a snapshot build, or move `syncConversationSessions` out of the read path.

**4. Global arrays dominate the payload (high).** ~300 KB of all-runs data per frame, of which **142 KB is `git_baseline_json`** that no snapshot code reads (events.ts:82, `select()` with no column projection). Fix: project columns like `WORKER_SNAPSHOT_COLUMNS` already does (persisted-snapshot.ts:102-114); paginate/limit `runs` and `plans`; split global catalog onto its own low-frequency channel.

**5. `messages` has no LIMIT (high).** events.ts:113 and persisted-snapshot.ts:264; full untruncated `content` via `message-records.ts:19-23`; `messageScope.complete` hardcoded `true` (events.ts:528). Unbounded growth over conversation lifetime, re-sent per frame.

**6. Whole-payload string diff (high).** events.ts:912-919 — one changed byte re-sends everything; suppression happens after all the cost. Two retained ~300 KB strings per client. Fix: per-array versioning and delta frames.

**7. Double `readPersistedEventRecords` in the runtime path (high).** events.ts:646 and 689 — ~40 queries where ~20 would do.

**8. Redundant double serialization (medium).** `payload-checksum.ts:3-8` stringifies + SHA-256, then events.ts:913 stringifies again. Memoize the serialized form with the checksum.

**9. Observer notifies unconditionally (medium).** `observer.ts:1287` is outside the `if (claimedTransition)` guard — every run generates a global fan-out every 5 s (`OBSERVER_INTERVAL_MS`, observer.ts:28) even when nothing changed. 10 runs = 2 notifications/sec of pure overhead. Line 1252-1256 also writes `updatedAt` unconditionally, which then defeats the string diff in finding 6.

**10. Cache keyed by `selectedRunId` with no global-data sharing (medium).** events.ts:599-601; two caches × 50 entries × ~300 KB ≈ 30 MB retained, FIFO-pruned (events.ts:627-635).

**11. Duplicate divergent snapshot builders (medium, correctness).** `persisted-snapshot.ts:229` vs `events.ts:566` differ in worker filtering (persisted-snapshot.ts:268-269 misses the `visibleRunIds` filter), queued-message status (persisted-snapshot.ts:286 still includes `delivering`, the bug events.ts:165-170 fixed), and payload shape. Guarantees checksum mismatch across the two, defeating the `notModified` fast path at events.ts:814-819. `PLANNING_REVIEW_FINDING_LIMIT` at persisted-snapshot.ts:35 is dead.

**12. `reconcilePersistedReloadZombies` runs 2 unguarded queries per build (low).** persisted-zombie-reconciler.ts:167 and 173-177 — write-capable reconciliation on a read path, called twice per runtime-enriched build.
````

## Claude thinking · 2026-08-05T10:33:27.191Z

I've confirmed the full flow: notifications trigger immediate wake-ups, which rebuild the complete snapshot and push it out. The `waitForEventStreamNotification` function short-circuits when the version changes, and there's no built-in rate limiting between snapshot pushes. The solution is to add server-side time-based coalescing that throttles full snapshot frames while letting cheaper named events like worker entry appends flow through immediately for transcript updates.
