## Claude thinking · 2026-08-05T20:37:13.272Z

I'm going to add a sentinel element at the bottom of the ScrollArea and use `scrollIntoView({ block: "end" })` to scroll to it, which the browser will resolve based on the element's actual position in the layout rather than relying on fixed measurements.

The real issue I'm seeing now is that the retry mechanism is permanently disabled after the first attempt — once `positionedRunId` is set during the same render pass, it won't try again even if the initial scroll landed short due to async content or layout shifts. That's the actual bug I need to fix, since it means if anything delays layout, there's no recovery.

The durable solution is to make the positioning self-correcting: after scrolling to the bottom, keep checking on subsequent frames whether we're actually at the bottom, and re-anchor if content has grown. The ResizeObserver already fires when content changes, so I can leverage that to trigger re-positioning while `shouldFollowLatest` is true and the user hasn't manually scrolled. The infrastructure for this retry already exists in `updateOutputBelowState` and `shouldConversationRetryInitialLatestPosition` — it's just being blocked by the `positionedRunId !== selectedRunId` gate.

The fix is to change the retry condition from "have we positioned once" to "are we still following the latest AND not actually at the bottom", which makes it self-correcting for any cause of landing short. Since `shouldFollowLatestRef` gets set to false as soon as the user scrolls up, gating the re-anchor on that flag keeps us from fighting the user's scroll.

The ResizeObserver can pin to bottom whenever `shouldFollowLatest` is true, which naturally follows content growth — the desired behavior for watching a live stream. There's a risk of an infinite loop (scrollTo → scroll event → updateFollowState → scrollTo), but the predicate requires `!atBottom` to fire, so once we reach the bottom it stops. Now I'm defining the new predicate function that takes the necessary flags and conditions. I see the issue now — when content grows below us, we're not at the bottom anymore, so `shouldConversationKeepFollowingLatest` returns false. That means `shouldFollowLatest` gets set to false, and then a scroll event won't trigger the re-anchor because we've already stopped following. The logic is getting tangled between detecting user scrolls versus detecting content growth.

The real fix is to track whether we were already following and only cancel that state when the user explicitly scrolls up. I'm modifying the function to accept a `wasFollowing` parameter so it can preserve the following state through content growth, then re-arm when they return to the bottom. This needs tests to ensure the behavior change doesn't break anything.

## Claude thinking · 2026-08-05T20:37:38.164Z

The test is currently asserting that a positioned run shouldn't retry, which is exactly what's causing the bug. I need to add `wasFollowing` to the keep-following logic so that content growth doesn't break the follow state—only an explicit upward scroll should. Then I'll replace the one-shot retry mechanism with a continuous reanchoring approach.

Defining the new predicates...

I'm wiring these into `useRunSelectionEffects` so that `updateOutputBelowState` uses the re-anchor predicate and `updateFollowState` passes the current follow state as context. The `previousScrollTopRef` gets updated after scrolling to the bottom, which should prevent loops since re-anchoring triggers a scroll event that eventually settles once we're at the bottom and content stops growing.

I need to remove `shouldConversationRetryInitialLatestPosition` since its semantics have changed with the new predicate, and update the tests accordingly. Let me implement this now.

  "old_string": "export function shouldConversationKeepFollowingLatest(\n  metrics: Pick<HTMLDivElement, \"scrollTop\" | \"clientHeight\" | \"scrollHeight\">,\n  previousScrollTop: number,\n) {\n  if (metrics.scrollTop < previousScrollTop) {\n    return false;\n  }\n\n  return shouldConversationFollowLatest(metrics);\n}\n\nexport function shouldConversationRetryInitialLatestPosition({\n  selectedRunId,\n  positionedRunId,\n  selectedRunHasOutput,\n  shouldFollowLatest,\n  metrics,\n}: {\n  selectedRunId: string | null;\n  positionedRunId: string | null;\n  selectedRunHasOutput: boolean;\n  shouldFollowLatest: boolean;\n  metrics: Pick<HTMLDivElement, \"clientHeight\" | \"scrollHeight\">;\n}) {\n  return Boolean(\n    selectedRunId\n    && selectedRunHasOutput\n    && positionedRunId !== selectedRunId\n    && shouldFollowLatest\n    && hasMeaningfulConversationOverflow(metrics),\n  );\n}",
  "new_string": "/**\n * Following the latest output is cancelled by the reader scrolling UP, and by\n * nothing else.\n *\n * This used to end with a bare `shouldConversationFollowLatest(metrics)`, which\n * meant content growing *beneath* the viewport also cancelled it — the reader\n * had not moved, but they were no longer within 8px of the bottom, so the app\n * decided they had chosen to stop following. `wasFollowing` keeps the intent\n * sticky; a reader who returns to the bottom re-arms it.\n */\nexport function shouldConversationKeepFollowingLatest(\n  metrics: Pick<HTMLDivElement, \"scrollTop\" | \"clientHeight\" | \"scrollHeight\">,\n  previousScrollTop: number,\n  wasFollowing = false,\n) {\n  if (metrics.scrollTop < previousScrollTop) {\n    return false;\n  }\n\n  return wasFollowing || shouldConversationFollowLatest(metrics);\n}\n\n/**\n * Re-pin to the bottom when we are supposed to be following but have drifted\n * off it — i.e. content grew below the viewport after we positioned.\n *\n * This replaces a one-shot \"retry the initial position\" check that was gated on\n * `positionedRunId !== selectedRunId` and therefore could fire at most once per\n * run, during the very pass that marked the run positioned. If that single\n * attempt measured short for any reason, the conversation stayed stranded\n * mid-transcript with no way to recover. Making the condition a property of the\n * current geometry rather than a one-time flag means it self-corrects for every\n * cause of landing short — late layout, async content, or a transcript window\n * that grew after an earlier `loadOlder`.\n *\n * Terminates naturally: once pinned to the bottom\n * `shouldConversationFollowLatest` is true and this returns false.\n */\nexport function shouldConversationReanchorToLatest({\n  selectedRunId,\n  selectedRunHasOutput,\n  shouldFollowLatest,\n  metrics,\n}: {\n  selectedRunId: string | null;\n  selectedRunHasOutput: boolean;\n  shouldFollowLatest: boolean;\n  metrics: Pick<HTMLDivElement, \"scrollTop\" | \"clientHeight\" | \"scrollHeight\">;\n}) {\n  return Boolean(\n    selectedRunId\n    && selectedRunHasOutput\n    && shouldFollowLatest\n    && hasMeaningfulConversationOverflow(metrics)\n    && !shouldConversationFollowLatest(metrics),\n  );\n}"
}

## Claude · 2026-08-05T20:45:27.520Z

Done. Everything green except the one pre-existing failure.

## What was wrong — it was my regression

The `content-visibility: auto` I added in the previous round. It tells the browser to skip layout for off-screen rows and substitute `contain-intrinsic-size` instead, which I set to `3rem` (48px). Real rows — markdown messages, tools with input/output panes — are often several hundred pixels.

The conversation finds the bottom by reading `viewport.scrollHeight` inside a **pre-paint layout effect** (`useRunSelectionEffects.ts:270`). At that moment every never-rendered row was contributing 48px instead of its true height, so `scrollHeight` was a large underestimate. It scrolled to a "bottom" far above the real one; then the browser painted, rows materialised at full height, and you were left stranded mid-transcript.

This hit direct-control conversations specifically because `Terminal` in `native` variant has no scroller of its own (`Terminal.tsx:2696` — `overflow-visible`), so those rows flow into the very viewport being measured.

**Your instinct about "it remembers" was right, just not the root cause.** `ConversationTranscriptManager.stateByRunId` is a Map cleared only by an explicit `reset()` (`ConversationTranscriptManager.ts:130`). Once you scroll back, `loadOlder` grows that run's window and it stays grown for the tab's lifetime. So the sessions you'd scrolled back in had the most rows — and therefore the largest underestimate. That's why it felt like it remembered where you'd scrolled to.

## Fixes

**1. Reverted the CSS.** Replaced with a comment explaining why it must not come back, and what would have to be true first. The old comment claimed "scroll height keeps working on real measurements" — that was simply wrong, and I want the next person to see the counter-argument rather than the same premise.

**2. Fixed the underlying fragility, which predates me.** Two real bugs in the follow logic:

- `shouldConversationKeepFollowingLatest` ended with a bare bottom check, so **content growing beneath you cancelled follow mode** — you hadn't moved, but you were no longer within 8px of the bottom, so the app decided you'd chosen to stop following. Follow is now sticky: only an upward scroll cancels it, and returning to the bottom re-arms it.

- The recovery path was `shouldConversationRetryInitialLatestPosition`, gated on `positionedRunId !== selectedRunId` — and line 276 marked the run positioned during that same pass. So it could fire **at most once per run, during the very pass that measured wrong**. If the first attempt landed short for any reason, there was no second chance. Replaced with `shouldConversationReanchorToLatest`, which is a property of current geometry rather than a one-time flag: if you're meant to be following and you've drifted off the bottom, re-pin. It self-corrects for late layout, async content, or a window grown by an earlier `loadOlder` — not just for my CSS. It terminates naturally, since once pinned the bottom check returns false.

Tests now pin the regression directly, including the case that was previously asserted as `false` (already-positioned run refusing to re-anchor), plus "reader scrolled up → never yank them back", and the sticky-follow behaviour. I also added a source assertion that the sticky flag is actually threaded through, since that wiring is what silently broke it.

## Verification

- `tsc` clean
- UI + app: **624 passed**
- server: **763 passed, 1 failed**
- api + runtime-api: **254 passed**
- lifecycle: **37 passed**
- eslint clean

The one failure is `syncConversationSessions > redelivers a queued answer as a normal prompt when the elicitation is already gone` — the same pre-existing failure from earlier, which I verified fails with my changes reverted and is unrelated to scrolling.

One note: my earlier attempt to run the whole suite in a single pass was killed with exit 137 (OOM). Running it in batches is fine — worth knowing if you hit the same thing.

I can't verify the actual scroll behaviour without driving the app; the predicates and wiring are proven by tests, but whether sessions now open at the bottom is something you'll feel immediately. This is client-side only, so a browser refresh is enough — no runner restart needed.
